sentences.zh: 序

translations.literal: Preface.
translations.idiomatic: Preface.

sentences.zh: 夫三才分位，室家之道克隆；

translations.literal: Now that the Three Powers each hold their allotted place, the moral pattern of household and family is firmly multiplied.
translations.idiomatic: When heaven, earth, and humanity stand in their proper stations, the way of family life takes deep root.

sentences.zh: 二族交歎，貞烈之風斯著。

translations.literal: The two clans exchange admiration, and the ethos of chaste steadfastness thus becomes conspicuous.
translations.idiomatic: Kin on both sides praise one another, and the aura of faithful integrity shines clear for all to see.

sentences.zh: 振高情而獨秀，魯冊於是飛華；

translations.literal: Those who stir lofty resolve and stand peerless bring glory to the Lu annals.
translations.idiomatic: Women of singular nobility lift the chronicles of Lu to brilliance.

sentences.zh: 挺峻節而孤標，周篇於焉騰茂。

translations.literal: Those who uphold austere integrity as a lone beacon lend splendor to the poems of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Their stern moral stature sets the Zhou hymns soaring.

sentences.zh: 徽烈兼劭，柔順無愆，隔代相望，諒非一緒。

translations.literal: Their splendid deeds pair with consummate grace; gentle submission without fault—though ages divide them, they answer one another across time: surely they are not cut from one cloth alone.
translations.idiomatic: They unite shining merit with flawless gentleness; generations apart, they still seem to speak to one another—not one simple lineage could contain them all.

sentences.zh: 然則虞興媯汭，夏盛塗山，有娀、有廣隆殷之業，大任、大姒衍昌姬之化，馬鄧恭儉，漢朝推德，宣昭懿淑，魏代揚芬，斯皆禮極中闈，義殊月室者矣。

translations.literal: Thus Yu rose from Guīruì, Xia flourished at Túshān; Yǒusōng and Yǒuguǎng built up Yin's greatness; Tài Rèn and Tài Sì extended the civilizing power that made the House of Zhōu flourish; the Mǎ and Dèng were reverent and frugal—Han acclaimed their virtue; Xuān's luminous goodness—Wei broadcast her fragrance: one and all they exhausted ritual within the royal women's quarters, their righteousness transcending that of the lunar chamber.
translations.idiomatic: From the rise of Yu at Guīruì to the glory of Xia at Tushan, from the mothers of Yin and Zhou who bore sage kings to the modest Ma and Deng ladies praised in Han, down to Wei exemplars of gentle wisdom—these women perfected ritual inside the palace women's quarters; their moral stature stands apart even from the storied "moon chamber."

sentences.zh: 至若恭薑誓節，孟母求仁，華率傅而經齊，樊授規而霸楚，譏文伯于奉劍，讓子發於分菽，少君之從約禮，孟光之符隱志，既昭婦則，且擅母儀。

translations.literal: As for reverent Jiāng swearing to keep her widowhood, Mèng's mother seeking goodness, Huà leading instruction and ordering Qi, Fàn handing down rules and making Chu a hegemon; reproaching Wénbó over the sword presentation, yielding to Zǐfā when dividing beans; Shaojūn's obedience that honored ritual, Mèngguāng's matching her husband's hidden resolve—they exemplified the wife's norm and excelled as models of motherhood.
translations.idiomatic: Think of reverent Jiāng's vow, Mèng's mother instructing her son, the tutors who steered Qi and Chu, the rebukes at court and the humility over a meal, Shaojūn's modest obedience, Mèngguāng's lamp-and-platter harmony: each engraved the wife's example and embodied a mother's standard.

sentences.zh: 子政緝之於前，元凱編之於後，具宣閨範，有裨陰訓。

translations.literal: Zǐzhèng gathered them at an earlier date, Yuánkǎi compiled them afterward, setting forth the entire repertoire of women's virtue and aiding instruction for the inner quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Liú Xiàng began the tradition; Dù Yù continued it, laying out models for the women's quarters and reinforcing lessons meant for the household.

sentences.zh: 故上從泰始，下迄恭安，一操可稱，一藝可紀，咸皆撰錄，為之傳云。

translations.literal: Therefore, from the Tàishǐ era down to the Gōng'ān reign, wherever a single virtue or a single skill deserved notice, we have recorded them all and fashioned these biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, from Western Jin's Taishi era through the Eastern Jin Gong'an years, every woman with one memorable deed or teachable talent has been gathered here.

sentences.zh: 或位極后妃，或事因夫子，各隨本傳，今所不錄。

translations.literal: Some rose to the rank of empress or consort; others are known through their husbands or sons—each already appears in the relevant standard biography and is not duplicated here.
translations.idiomatic: Queens and imperial consorts, or stories told chiefly through husbands and sons, remain in those main biographies and are omitted from this collection.

sentences.zh: 在諸偽國，暫阻王猷，天下之善，足以懲勸，亦同搜次，附於篇末。

translations.literal: Among the various short-lived regimes that briefly blocked the kingly enterprise, whatever good remained in the realm still serves to admonish and encourage; we have searched these out as well and appended them at the end of the chapter.
translations.idiomatic: Even under the so-called usurper houses that momentarily interrupted imperial rule, exemplary conduct still deserves to be remembered; those entries are gathered at the close of this chapter.

sentences.zh: 羊耽妻辛憲英

translations.literal: Xīn Xiànyīng, wife of Yáng Dān
translations.idiomatic: Xīn Xiànyīng, wife of Yáng Dān

sentences.zh: 羊耽妻辛氏，字憲英，隴西人，魏侍中毗之女也。

translations.literal: The wife of Yáng Dān, née Xīn, courtesy name Xiànyīng, was a native of Lǒngxī and the daughter of the Wei Palace Attendant Xīn Pí.
translations.idiomatic: Yáng Dān's wife, Lady Xīn Xiànyīng of Longxi, was the daughter of the Wei courtier Xīn Pí.

sentences.zh: 聰朗有才鑒。

translations.literal: She was bright, clear-sighted, and possessed judgment.
translations.idiomatic: She was perceptive, quick-witted, and astute.

sentences.zh: 初，魏文帝得立為太子，抱毗項謂之曰：「辛君知我喜不？

translations.literal: At first, when Emperor Wen of Wei was established as heir apparent, he embraced Pí around the neck and said to him, "Lord Xīn, do you know how pleased I am?"
translations.idiomatic: When Cáo Pī first became crown prince, he threw his arms around Xīn Pí's neck and asked, "Do you know how happy this makes me?"

sentences.zh: 」毗以告憲英，憲英歎曰：「太子，代君主宗廟社稷者也。

translations.literal: Pí reported this to Xiànyīng, who sighed and said, "The crown prince is he who will replace the ruler and take charge of the altars of state and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Xīn Pí told his daughter; she sighed and replied, "The heir is the man who will succeed the throne and bear the shrines of realm and soil on his shoulders."

sentences.zh: 代君不可以不戚，主國不可以不懼，宜戚而喜，何以能久！

translations.literal: To replace the ruler one ought not be gleeful; to lord over the state one ought not be careless—yet he is pleased where he should be apprehensive: how can this long endure!
translations.idiomatic: He should dread inheriting the throne and tremble for the realm—yet he rejoices. Such a house cannot last."

sentences.zh: 魏其不昌乎？」

translations.literal: Will not Wei soon cease to flourish?"
translations.idiomatic: His line will not prosper for long."

sentences.zh: 弟敞為大將軍曹爽參軍，宣帝將誅爽，因其從魏帝出而閉城門，爽司馬魯芝率府兵斬關赴爽，呼敞同去。

translations.literal: Her younger brother Chǎng served as army adviser to General-in-Chief Cáo Shuǎng. When Emperor Xuān was about to execute Shuǎng, he seized the moment when Shuang accompanied the Wei emperor on an outing to shut the city gates; Shuǎng's Major Lǔ Zhī led the garrison troops to cut through the bar and rush to Shuang, shouting for Chǎng to flee with them.
translations.idiomatic: Her brother Yáng Chǎng was an adviser to Cáo Shuǎng. As Sima Yi prepared to purge Shuǎng, the capital gates were closed while the emperor was away; Lǔ Zhī hacked through a gate and urged Chǎng to ride with Shuǎng's guard.

sentences.zh: 敞懼，問憲英曰：「天子在外，太傅閉城門，人云將不利國家，於事可得爾乎？

translations.literal: Chǎng was afraid and asked Xiànyīng, "The Son of Heaven is outside the walls, the Grand Tutor has sealed the gates—people say this bodes ill for the dynasty; can matters truly have come to this?"
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Chǎng asked his sister, "The emperor is outside the city and the regent has barred the gates—rumor says the state is in peril. Is it really as dire as they claim?"

sentences.zh: 」憲英曰：「事有不可知，然以吾度之，太傅殆不得不爾。

translations.literal: Xiànyīng replied, "Events may be unknowable, yet by my reckoning the Grand Tutor can hardly do otherwise.
translations.idiomatic: "Nothing is certain," she said, "but I judge Sima Yi has no choice but to act."

sentences.zh: 明皇帝臨崩，把太傅臂，屬以後事，此言猶在朝士之耳。

translations.literal: When Emperor Míng lay dying, he grasped the Grand Tutor's arm and entrusted him with the aftermath—those words still ring in the ears of the courtiers.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming on his deathbed clasped Sima Yi's arm and entrusted him with the boy emperor—the court still remembers that charge."

sentences.zh: 且曹爽與太傅俱受寄託之任，而獨專權勢，於王室不忠，於人道不直，此舉不過以誅爽耳。

translations.literal: Moreover, Cáo Shuǎng and the Grand Tutor alike received the late emperor's commission, yet Shuǎng alone monopolizes power; toward the royal house he is disloyal, and by human standards he is in the wrong—this move aims at nothing beyond executing Shuǎng.
translations.idiomatic: Cáo Shuǎng shares the regency yet hoards authority; he is false to the throne and unjust by every moral measure—Sima Yi is simply moving to cut him down."

sentences.zh: 」敞曰：「然則敞無出乎？

translations.literal: Chǎng said, "Then must I not go out?"
translations.idiomatic: "So I should stay home?"

sentences.zh: 」憲英曰：「安可以不出！

translations.literal: Xiànyīng answered, "How can you fail to go out!"
translations.idiomatic: "You must go—how could you refuse?"

sentences.zh: 職守，人之大義也。

translations.literal: Office is among the greatest obligations binding a person.
translations.idiomatic: Duty to one's post is a paramount obligation.

sentences.zh: 凡人在難，猶或恤之；

translations.literal: Ordinary folk will still pity someone in distress;
translations.idiomatic: Even common people pity comrades in danger;

sentences.zh: 為人執鞭而棄其事，不祥也。

translations.literal: to serve another as groom yet abandon that charge bodes ill.
translations.idiomatic: to accept another's pay and desert him in crisis invites disaster.

sentences.zh: 且為人任，為人死，親昵之職也，汝從眾而已。

translations.literal: Moreover, when you accept responsibility for someone, you should be prepared to die for him—the office of an intimate adviser demands no less; follow the crowd and go.
translations.idiomatic: You took his stipend; you owe him your life in a trusted adviser's role—go with the rest and do your part."

sentences.zh: 」敞遂出。

translations.literal: Chǎng therefore rode out.
translations.idiomatic: Chǎng went.

sentences.zh: 宣帝果誅爽。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuān indeed executed Shuǎng.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi did execute Cáo Shuǎng.

sentences.zh: 事定後，敞歎曰：「吾不謀于姊，幾不獲於義！」

translations.literal: After order was restored, Chǎng sighed, "Had I not consulted my elder sister, I would almost have fallen short of righteousness!"
translations.idiomatic: When the dust settled he said, "Without my sister's counsel I would nearly have failed decency itself!"

sentences.zh: 其後鐘會為鎮西將軍，憲英謂耽從子祜曰：「鐘士季何故西出？

translations.literal: Later, when Zhōng Huì became General Who Guards the West, Xiànyīng said to Dān's nephew Hù, "Why is Zhòng Shìjì marching west?"
translations.idiomatic: When Zhōng Huì received the western command, she asked her cousin-in-law Yáng Hù why Zhòng Shìjì was headed into Shu.

sentences.zh: 」祐曰：「將為滅蜀也。

translations.literal: Hù answered, "He goes to destroy Shu."
translations.idiomatic: "To conquer Shu," Hù replied.

sentences.zh: 」憲英曰：「會在事縱恣，非持久處下之道，吾畏其有他志也。

translations.literal: Xiànyīng said, "Zhōng Huì indulges his whims in office; he cannot long remain subordinate—I fear he harbors other designs.
translations.idiomatic: "Zhōng Huì has always done as he pleased," she warned. "No man like that stays content as a subordinate—mark my words: he is nursing larger ambitions."

sentences.zh: 」及會將行，請其子琇為參軍，憲英憂曰：「他日吾為國憂，今日難至吾家矣。

translations.literal: When Huì was about to depart, he asked her son Xiù to join him as adviser; Xiànyīng anxiously said, "Yesterday I worried for the realm; today calamity reaches my own gate.
translations.idiomatic: As Huì prepared to leave he pressed her son Yáng Xiù into his staff. "Yesterday I feared for the country," she said; "today trouble has come to our household."

sentences.zh: 」琇固請于文帝，帝不聽。

translations.literal: Xiù importuned Emperor Wén again and again, but the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Xiù pleaded with Sima Zhāo; the prince refused to excuse him.

sentences.zh: 憲英謂琇曰：「行矣，戒之！

translations.literal: Xiànyīng told Xiù, "Go—but heed my warning!
translations.idiomatic: "Then go," she told Xiù, "and remember this:"

sentences.zh: 古之君子入則致孝於親，出則致節于國；

translations.literal: The gentlemen of old showed filial devotion at home and displayed steadfast loyalty abroad;
translations.idiomatic: The ancients honored parents in private and served the state with integrity abroad;

sentences.zh: 在職思其所司，在義思其所立，不遺父母憂患而已。

translations.literal: in office they pondered their duties; in matters of principle they pondered the stand they must take—doing no more than sparing their parents added sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: on duty they weighed their responsibilities; in moral crises they weighed the right course—never bringing shame or worry upon family."

sentences.zh: 軍旅之間可以濟者，其惟仁恕乎！

translations.literal: In the camps of war, perhaps nothing sees you through but benevolence and forbearance!
translations.idiomatic: Amid armies and intrigue, only kindness and restraint will save you."

sentences.zh: 」會至蜀果反，琇竟以全歸。

translations.literal: Huì did rebel after reaching Shu, yet Xiù returned home unharmed.
translations.idiomatic: Huì did rise in rebellion; Xiù nevertheless came home alive.

sentences.zh: 祜嘗送錦被，憲英嫌其華，反而覆之，其明鑒儉約如此。

translations.literal: When Hù once sent a brocade quilt, Xiànyīng found it too sumptuous and turned it lining outward—such was her clear judgment and frugality.
translations.idiomatic: Hù once gifted a silk quilt; she deemed it ostentatious and flipped it to the plain side—her taste for simplicity ran that deep.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十九。

translations.literal: She died at the age of seventy-nine.
translations.idiomatic: She died at seventy-nine.

sentences.zh: 杜有道妻嚴憲

translations.literal: Yán Xiàn, wife of Dù Yǒudào
translations.idiomatic: Yán Xiàn, wife of Dù Yǒudào

sentences.zh: 杜有道妻嚴氏，字憲，京兆人也。

translations.literal: The wife of Dù Yǒudào, née Yán, courtesy name Xiàn, came from the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yán Xiàn of Jingzhao was married to Dù Yǒudào.

sentences.zh: 貞淑有識量。

translations.literal: Chaste, mild, and possessed of judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Virtuous, poised, and far-sighted.

sentences.zh: 年十三，適於杜氏，十八而嫠居。

translations.literal: At thirteen she married into the Dù family; at eighteen she was widowed.
translations.idiomatic: She married into the Du clan at thirteen and was widowed at eighteen.

sentences.zh: 子植、女韡並孤藐，憲雖少，誓不改節，撫育二子，教以禮度，植遂顯名于時，韡亦有淑德，傳玄求為繼室，憲便許之。

translations.literal: Her son Zhí and daughter Wěi were both still tiny; though Xiàn was young, she swore never to remarry, rearing both children according to ritual norms—Zhí rose to renown in his day, Wěi acquired worthy virtue, and when Fù Xuán sought her as a second wife she consented.
translations.idiomatic: She raised her orphaned son Zhí and daughter Wěi, refusing remarriage though barely more than a girl; Zhí became famous, Wěi grew admirable, and she agreed when Fù Xuán asked to marry her.

sentences.zh: 時玄與何晏、鄧揚不穆，晏等每欲害之，時人莫肯共婚。

translations.literal: At that time Xuán was on bad terms with Hé Yàn and Dèng Yáng; Yàn and his faction repeatedly plotted to harm him, and no one dared contract marriage with him.
translations.idiomatic: Fù Xuán feuded with Hé Yàn and Dèng Yáng, who kept plotting against him—nobody would ally with Xuán by marriage.

sentences.zh: 及憲許玄，內外以為憂懼。

translations.literal: When Xiàn promised Xiū to Xuān, her whole clan trembled with anxiety.
translations.idiomatic: Her kinsmen were terrified when she accepted.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「何、鄧執權，必為玄害，亦由排山壓卵，以湯沃雪耳，奈何與之為親？

translations.literal: Some said, "Hé and Dèng hold power; they are sure to ruin Xuán—against them it would be like toppling a mountain onto an egg or pouring boiling water on snow—why bind yourself to such a match?"
translations.idiomatic: "Hé and Dèng control the court—they will crush Xuán as surely as a landslide flattens an egg. Why tie our family to his?"

sentences.zh: 」憲曰：「爾知其一，不知其他。

translations.literal: Xiàn replied, "You grasp one side and miss the rest.
translations.idiomatic: "You see only half the picture,"

sentences.zh: 晏等驕移，必當自敗，司馬太傅獸睡耳，吾恐卵破雪銷，行自有在。

translations.literal: Yàn and his ilk are arrogant and unsteady—they will destroy themselves; Grand Tutor Sima only feigns sleep—I suspect the egg will crack and the snow melt of its own accord soon enough.
translations.idiomatic: she answered. "Those men are bloated with pride and will fall of themselves; Sima Yi merely seems to slumber. Their league will shatter like eggshell and melt like snow—you will see."

sentences.zh: 」遂與玄為婚。

translations.literal: She therefore married Xiū to Xuán.
translations.idiomatic: She went ahead with the wedding.

sentences.zh: 晏等尋亦為宣帝所誅。

translations.literal: Before long Yàn and the others were executed by Emperor Xuān.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Hé Yàn's faction fell to Sima Yi's purge.

sentences.zh: 植後為南安太守。

translations.literal: Zhí later became governor of Nán'ān.
translations.idiomatic: Her son Du Zhí became prefect of Nan'an.

sentences.zh: 植從兄預為秦州刺史，被誣，徵還，憲與預書戒之曰：「諺-{云}-忍辱至三公。

translations.literal: Zhí's elder cousin Yù served as Inspector of Qín province; when he was slandered and recalled, Xiàn wrote to caution him, saying, "The proverb runs: enduring humiliation leads to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Her nephew Du Yù, governor of Qin, faced false charges and recall; she wrote, "They say patience through disgrace carries a man to the three highest offices."

sentences.zh: 卿今可謂辱矣，能忍之，公是卿坐。

translations.literal: You may now count yourself humiliated; endure it, and the ducal seats await you.
translations.idiomatic: "You are certainly humbled now; bear it, and those exalted posts will yet be yours."

sentences.zh: 」預後果為儀同三司。

translations.literal: Yù indeed rose to be Commissioner Equal to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yù eventually gained rank equal to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 玄前妻子咸年六歲，嘗隨其繼母省憲，謂咸曰：「汝千里駒也，必當遠至。

translations.literal: Xuán's son by a previous wife, Xián, was six years old when he once accompanied his stepmother to visit Xiàn; she told Xián, "You are a colt meant to run a thousand leagues—you will surely travel far.
translations.idiomatic: Xuán's six-year-old son Xián visited with his stepmother; Xiàn said, "You are a thousand-li foal—you will go far."

sentences.zh: 」以其妹之女妻之。

translations.literal: She gave him her niece as wife.
translations.idiomatic: She married her niece to him.

sentences.zh: 咸後亦有名於海內。

translations.literal: Xián later became celebrated throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Xián later won fame empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 其知人之鑒如此。

translations.literal: Such was her talent for reading men.
translations.idiomatic: Thus keen was her judgment of people.

sentences.zh: 年六十六卒。

translations.literal: She died at sixty-six.
translations.idiomatic: She died at sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 王渾妻鍾琰

translations.literal: Zhōng Yǎn, wife of Wáng Hún
translations.idiomatic: Zhōng Yǎn, wife of Wáng Hún

sentences.zh: 王渾妻鍾氏，字琰，潁川人，魏太傅繇曾孫也。

translations.literal: The wife of Wáng Hún, née Zhōng, courtesy name Yǎn, was from Yǐngchuān and the great-granddaughter of Wei Grand Tutor Zhōng Yóu.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhōng Yǎn of Yingchuan, great-granddaughter of Zhōng Yóu, married Wáng Hún.

sentences.zh: 父徽，黃門郎。

translations.literal: Her father Huī was a Gentleman at the Yellow Gates.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Zhōng Huī was a palace gate tender.

sentences.zh: 琰數歲能屬文，及長，聰慧弘雅，博覽記籍。

translations.literal: Yǎn could compose essays while still a child; grown, she was clever, refined, and widely read.
translations.idiomatic: She wrote essays as a girl; as a woman she was brilliant, graceful, and learned.

sentences.zh: 美容止，善嘯詠，禮儀法度為中表所則。

translations.literal: Lovely in bearing, skilled in whistling and song, her deportment became the model for cousins on both sides.
translations.idiomatic: Graceful and skilled in song, she set the tone for her extended kin.

sentences.zh: 既適渾，生濟。

translations.literal: After she married Hún she bore Jì.
translations.idiomatic: She bore Wáng Jì after marrying Hún.

sentences.zh: 渾嘗共琰坐，濟趨庭而過，渾欣然曰：「生子如此，足慰人心。

translations.literal: Once when Hún sat with Yǎn, Jì hurried past the courtyard; Hún beamed, "To father such a son is comfort enough for any heart.
translations.idiomatic: One day Jì crossed the yard while his parents conversed; Hún beamed, "A son like this heartens a father."

sentences.zh: 」琰笑曰：「若使新婦得配參軍，生子故不翅如此。

translations.literal: Yǎn smiled and said, "Had your new wife been matched with your brother the army aide, our sons would have been more than merely this.
translations.idiomatic: Yǎn smiled. "Had I married your younger brother the military aide, our sons would have been no less remarkable."

sentences.zh: 」參軍，謂渾中弟淪也。

translations.literal: The army aide refers to Hún's middle brother Lún.
translations.idiomatic: "Army aide" meant his brother Wáng Lún.

sentences.zh: 琰女亦有才淑，為求賢夫。

translations.literal: Yǎn's daughter was likewise talented and virtuous; Yǎn sought a worthy husband for her.
translations.idiomatic: Her daughter was equally gifted; Yǎn hunted for a worthy son-in-law.

sentences.zh: 時有兵家子甚俊，濟欲妻之，白琰，琰曰：「要令我見之。

translations.literal: A military man's son was notably handsome; Jì wished to marry her to him and informed Yǎn, who said, "I must see him myself.
translations.idiomatic: A junior officer's son seemed splendid; Jì proposed the match, but Yǎn insisted on inspecting him.

sentences.zh: 」濟令此兵與群小雜處，琰自幃中察之，既而謂濟曰：「緋衣者非汝所拔乎？

translations.literal: Jì had the fellow mingle with low attendants; from behind a curtain Yǎn studied him, then told Jì, "The man in scarlet is not the one you picked?"
translations.idiomatic: She watched from behind a screen as he stood among servants. "The man in red," she asked Jì, "isn't he your choice?"

sentences.zh: 」濟曰：「是。

translations.literal: Jì said, "Yes."
translations.idiomatic: "Yes."

sentences.zh: 」琰曰：「此人才足拔萃，然地寒壽促，不足展其器用，不可與婚。

translations.literal: Yǎn replied, "His talent may lift him above the crowd, yet his station is lowly and his fate short—he cannot realize his gifts; do not give him our daughter.
translations.idiomatic: "He has ability," she said, "but mean birth and a brief span—his gifts will never fully bloom. This match will not do."

sentences.zh: 」遂止。

translations.literal: The matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Jì abandoned the idea.

sentences.zh: 其人數年果亡。

translations.literal: Within a few years the man indeed died.
translations.idiomatic: The young officer died just as she predicted.

sentences.zh: 琰明鑒遠識，皆此類也。

translations.literal: So ran her prescience in such matters.
translations.idiomatic: Her foresight always proved so exact.

sentences.zh: 渾弟湛妻郝氏亦有德行，琰雖貴門，與郝雅相親重，郝不以賤下琰，琰不以貴陵郝，時人稱「鐘夫人之禮，郝夫人之法」-{云}-。

translations.literal: Hún's younger brother Zhàn's wife, Lady Hǎo, was likewise virtuous; though Yǎn came from an exalted clan, she treated Hǎo with sincere respect, while Hǎo did not demean herself before Yǎn nor did Yǎn lord it over Hǎo—people of the time praised "the courtesy of Lady Zhōng, the discipline of Lady Hǎo."
translations.idiomatic: Zhàn's wife Lady Hǎo was equally ethical; noble-born Yǎn cherished her without condescension, and Hǎo never bowed obsequiously—contemporaries spoke of "Lady Zhōng's ritual grace and Lady Hǎo's household law."

sentences.zh: 鄭袤妻曹氏

translations.literal: Lady Cáo, wife of Zhèng Mào
translations.idiomatic: Lady Cáo, wife of Zhèng Mào

sentences.zh: 鄭袤妻曹氏。

translations.literal: Lady Cáo, wife of Zhèng Mào.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Cáo, wife of Zheng Mao.

sentences.zh: 魯國薛人也。

translations.literal: She was a native of Xue in the state of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: She came from Xue in Lu.

sentences.zh: 袤先娶孫氏，早亡，娉之為繼室。

translations.literal: Mào had first married the Lady Sūn, who died young; he then took Lady Cáo as his successor wife.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Mao's first wife Lady Sun died young; he then married Lady Cao as his successor.

sentences.zh: 事舅姑甚孝，躬紡織之勤，以充奉養，至於叔妹群娣之間，盡其禮節，咸得歡心。

translations.literal: She served her parents-in-law with utmost filial duty, personally spinning and weaving to supply their needs; among sisters-in-law and junior wives she observed every courtesy and won every heart.
translations.idiomatic: She cared for her parents-in-law devotedly, weaving to support them, and treated sisters-in-law with such tact that the household adored her.

sentences.zh: 及袤為司空，其子默等又顯朝列，時人稱其榮貴。

translations.literal: When Mào became Minister of Works and his sons Mò and the others rose to prominent posts at court, contemporaries lauded their glory.
translations.idiomatic: When Mao rose to Minister of Works and his sons Mo gained high office, people called them splendid.

sentences.zh: 曹氏深懼盛滿，每默等升進，輒憂之形於聲色。

translations.literal: Lady Cáo deeply feared the peril of peak fortune; whenever Mò and the others won promotion, worry showed in her voice and face.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Lady Cao dreaded excess: each promotion for Mo shadowed her face with dread.

sentences.zh: 然食無重味，服浣濯之衣，袤等所獲祿秩，曹氏必班散親姻，務令周給，家無餘貲。

translations.literal: Nevertheless she ate no rich fare and wore only washed clothes; whatever salary Mao's sons earned she shared among kin until none lacked, leaving nothing hoarded at home.
translations.idiomatic: She ate plainly, dressed plainly, and scattered every salary her sons earned to needy relatives until nothing remained in the coffers.

sentences.zh: 初，孫氏瘞于黎陽，及袤薨，議者以久喪難舉，欲不合葬。

translations.literal: At first Lady Sūn was buried at Líyáng; when Mào died, advisors argued that the long delay since her burial made joint interment impractical.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Sun lay at Liyang; after Mao's death some argued the years since her death made joint burial impractical.

sentences.zh: 曹氏曰：「孫氏元妃，理當從葬，不可使孤魂無所依邪。

translations.literal: Lady Cáo said, "Lady Sūn was the principal wife—by right she should follow him to the tomb; we cannot leave a lone spirit with nowhere to rest.
translations.idiomatic: "Lady Sun was his first wife," Cao insisted. "She belongs beside him—we cannot strand her ghost unattended."

sentences.zh: 」於是備吉凶導從之儀以迎之，具衣衾几筵，親執雁行之禮，聞者莫不歎息，以為趙姬之下叔隗，不足稱也。

translations.literal: She therefore prepared full funeral escort with auspicious and inauspicious regalia to welcome the earlier burial, supplied garments, cushions, and offerings, and herself performed the goose-bearing ritual—those who heard it sighed, deeming even Zhào Jī's deference to Shūwéi unworthy of comparison.
translations.idiomatic: She staged the full procession, draped the bier, and walked the ritual herself—onlookers wept, declaring Zhao Ji's famous homage to Shuwei paled beside this.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十三。

translations.literal: She died at eighty-three.
translations.idiomatic: She died at eighty-three.

sentences.zh: 湣懷太子妃王惠風

translations.literal: Wáng Huìfēng, consort of Crown Prince Mǐnhuái
translations.idiomatic: Wáng Huìfēng, consort of Crown Prince Minhuai

sentences.zh: 湣懷太子妃王氏，太尉衍女也，字惠風。

translations.literal: The consort of Crown Prince Mǐnhuái, née Wáng, was the daughter of Grand Commandant Yǎn; her courtesy name was Huìfēng.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wang Huifeng, daughter of Minister Wang Yan, was consort to Crown Prince Yu.

sentences.zh: 貞婉有志節。

translations.literal: Chaste, gentle, and strong in resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Virtuous, graceful, and iron-willed.

sentences.zh: 太子既廢居於金墉，衍請絕婚，惠風號哭而歸，行路為之流涕。

translations.literal: After the heir was deposed and confined at Jīnyōng, Yǎn sought to annul the marriage; Huìfēng wailed as she returned home, and wayfarers wept for her.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima's faction deposed the prince at Jinyong, Wang Yan tried to dissolve the marriage; Huifeng sobbed her way home while strangers wept along the road.

sentences.zh: 及劉曜陷洛陽，以惠風賜其將喬屬，屬將妻之。

translations.literal: When Liu Yao captured Luoyang, he presented Huifeng to his general Qiao Shu, who intended to take her as wife.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Yao seized Luoyang, he handed Wang Huifeng to his officer Qiao Shu, who meant to marry her.

sentences.zh: 惠風拔劍距屬曰：「吾太尉公女，皇太子妃，義不為逆胡所辱。

translations.literal: Huifeng drew her sword and barred Shu, declaring, "I am the daughter of the Grand Commandant and consort of the crown prince—I will not suffer dishonor at the hands of rebel barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: She leveled her blade at Shu and cried that she was Wang Yan's daughter and the crown prince's consort—she would die before submitting to a traitorous Hu chieftain.

sentences.zh: 」屬遂害之。

translations.literal: Shu thereupon killed her.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Shu murdered her.

sentences.zh: 鄭休妻石氏

translations.literal: Lady Shi, wife of Zhèng Xiū
translations.idiomatic: Lady Shi, wife of Zheng Xiu

sentences.zh: 鄭休妻石氏，不知何許人也。

translations.literal: Lady Shi, wife of Zhèng Xiū, was of unknown origin.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xiu's wife Lady Shi—her homeland is unrecorded.

sentences.zh: 少有德操，年十餘歲，鄉邑稱之。

translations.literal: From youth she possessed virtue and integrity; before she was twenty the district praised her.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a girl she had sterling character, and the countryside praised her before she turned twenty.

sentences.zh: 既歸鄭氏，為九族所重。

translations.literal: Once married into the Zhèng clan, the nine kinship circles held her in esteem.
translations.idiomatic: After she entered the Zheng family, every branch of the clan respected her.

sentences.zh: 休前妻女既幼，又休父布臨終，有庶子沈生，命棄之，石氏曰：「奈何使舅之胤不存乎！

translations.literal: Xiū's daughter by his first wife was still a child, and when Xiū's father Bù lay dying he had a bastard son Shēn whom he ordered cast aside; Lady Shi said, "How can we allow our father-in-law's bloodline to perish!"
translations.idiomatic: Her husband's little daughter by an earlier wife still needed care, and Xiu's dying father had ordered a maid-born son Shen abandoned; Lady Shi protested, "We cannot let our father-in-law's heir vanish."

sentences.zh: 」遂養沈及前妻女。

translations.literal: She therefore raised Shēn together with the daughter of the first wife.
translations.idiomatic: She reared both Shen and the first wife's girl.

sentences.zh: 力不兼舉，九年之中，三不舉子。

translations.literal: Her strength could not sustain everything at once; across nine years she thrice failed to bring infants successfully to term.
translations.idiomatic: The strain was so great that for nine years running she could not carry a birth to completion while raising those children.

sentences.zh: 陶侃母湛氏

translations.literal: Zhàn Zhàn's mother, Lady Zhàn
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhan, mother of Tao Kan

sentences.zh: 陶侃母湛氏，豫章新淦人也。

translations.literal: The mother of Tao Kan, née Zhàn, came from Xingan in Yùzhāng.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan's mother, Lady Zhan of Xingan in Yuzhang commandery.

sentences.zh: 初，侃父丹娉為妾，生侃，而陶氏貧賤，湛氏每紡績資給之，使交結勝己。

translations.literal: At first Kan's father Dān took Lady Zhàn as a concubine and she bore Kan; the Tao household was poor and lowly, yet Lady Zhàn constantly spun thread to supply him and urged him to befriend men superior to himself.
translations.idiomatic: Kan's father took her as a concubine; though the Taos were destitute, she spun for him and paid his social calls so he could network upward.

sentences.zh: 侃少為尋陽縣吏，嘗監魚梁，以一坩鮓遺母。

translations.literal: Kan in youth was a clerk in Xunyang county and once supervised a fish weir, sending his mother a jar of salted fish.
translations.idiomatic: As a young county clerk in Xunyang he oversaw a fishery and mailed her salted fish.

sentences.zh: 湛氏封鮓及書，責侃曰：「爾為吏，以官物遺我，非惟不能益吾，乃以增吾憂矣。

translations.literal: Lady Zhàn returned the jar with a letter and rebuked Kan: "You hold office yet send me government property—not only does this fail to help me, it only deepens my sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: She sent the jar back with a scolding: official supplies were not gifts—he only added to her shame.

sentences.zh: 」鄱陽孝廉範逵寓宿于侃，時大雪，湛氏乃徹所臥親薦，自銼給其馬，又密截發賣與鄰人，供肴饌。

translations.literal: When the Xiàolián graduate Fàn Kuí lodged with Kan during a journey, a heavy snow fell; Lady Zhàn tore up the straw mat she slept on to feed his horses, secretly clipped her hair to sell to neighbors, and prepared a feast.
translations.idiomatic: When scholar Fan Kui stayed overnight, blizzard snow fell; she shredded her bedding for his horses, sold her shorn hair for cash, and laid out a banquet worthy of a gentleman.

sentences.zh: 逵聞之，歎息曰：「非此母不生此子！

translations.literal: When Kuí learned of it he sighed, "Without such a mother such a son would never arise!"
translations.idiomatic: Fan Kui marveled, "No mother like this, no son like him!"

sentences.zh: 」侃竟以功名顯。

translations.literal: Kan indeed rose to fame and merit.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan rose to glory.

sentences.zh: 賈渾妻宗氏

translations.literal: Lady Zōng, wife of Jiǎ Hún
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zong, wife of Jia Hun

sentences.zh: 賈渾妻宗氏，不知何許人也。

translations.literal: Lady Zōng, wife of Jiǎ Hún, was of unknown origin.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Hun's wife Lady Zong—her birthplace is unknown.

sentences.zh: 渾為介休令，被劉元海將喬晞攻破，死之。

translations.literal: Hún served as magistrate of Jiexiu when Qiáo Xī, general of Liu Yuanhai, stormed the town; Hún died in the fighting.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Jiexiu he fell when Liu Yuan's officer Qiao Xi stormed the city.

sentences.zh: 宗氏有姿色，晞欲納之。

translations.literal: Lady Zōng was lovely of face; Xī wished to marry her.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Xi coveted her beauty and meant to wed her.

sentences.zh: 宗氏罵曰：「屠各奴！

translations.literal: Lady Zōng cursed him: "Tuge slave!"
translations.idiomatic: She spat back, "Tuge slave!"

sentences.zh: 豈有害人之夫而欲加無禮，于爾安乎？

translations.literal: Could you murder another woman's husband yet expect me to submit—would that bring you any honor?
translations.idiomatic: You slew my lord yet crave me—does that sit well even with you?

sentences.zh: 何不促殺我！

translations.literal: Better kill me now!
translations.idiomatic: Strike me down at once!

sentences.zh: 」因仰天大哭。

translations.literal: She then lifted her face and wailed to heaven.
translations.idiomatic: She threw back her head and screamed at the sky.

sentences.zh: 晞遂害之，時年二十餘。

translations.literal: Xī murdered her; she was just over twenty.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Xi killed her; she was barely twenty.

sentences.zh: 梁緯妻辛氏

translations.literal: Lady Xīn, wife of Liáng Wěi
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xin, wife of Liang Wei

sentences.zh: 梁緯妻辛氏，隴西狄道人也。

translations.literal: The wife of Liáng Wěi, née Xīn, came from Didao in Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Wei's wife Lady Xin of Didao in Longxi.

sentences.zh: 緯為散騎常侍，西都陷沒，為劉曜所害。

translations.literal: Wěi served as Cavalry Attendant in Regular Service; when the western capital fell he was killed by Liu Yao.
translations.idiomatic: He was an imperial attendant when Chang'an fell to Liu Yao and died in the sack.

sentences.zh: 辛氏有殊色，曜將妻之。

translations.literal: Lady Xīn possessed extraordinary beauty; Yao's officers wished to marry her.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao's men coveted her looks and meant to take her.

sentences.zh: 辛氏據地大哭，仰謂曜曰：「妾聞男以義烈，女不再醮。

translations.literal: Lady Xīn beat the earth and wailed, then looked up at Yao and said, "I have heard that men live by righteous valor and that a woman does not take a second husband.
translations.idiomatic: She threw herself to the ground, then faced Liu Yao: men die for honor; widows do not remarry.

sentences.zh: 妾夫已死，理無獨全。

translations.literal: My husband is dead; by principle I cannot survive alone.
translations.idiomatic: Her husband was gone—she had no wish to outlive him alone.

sentences.zh: 且婦人再辱，明公亦安用哉！

translations.literal: Moreover, if a woman suffers dishonor twice, what use would she be to you, my lord!
translations.idiomatic: Besides, a twice-shamed woman would disgrace even your hall—what good would she be?

sentences.zh: 乞即就死。

translations.literal: I beg to die at once.
translations.idiomatic: Let me die now.

sentences.zh: 下事舅姑。

translations.literal: To linger would betray the parents-in-law I ought to serve.
translations.idiomatic: Living on would mock the very in-laws I owe duty to.

sentences.zh: 」逐號哭不止。

translations.literal: "Thus she wailed without ceasing.
translations.idiomatic: Thus she wailed on without stopping.

sentences.zh: 曜曰：「貞婦也，任之。

translations.literal: Yao declared, "A woman of chaste fidelity—let her go her way."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao said only, "A faithful wife—leave her be."

sentences.zh: 」自縊而死。

translations.literal: She strangled herself.
translations.idiomatic: She hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 曜以禮葬之。

translations.literal: Yao buried her with ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao gave her an honorable burial.

sentences.zh: 許延妻杜氏

translations.literal: Lady Dù, wife of Xǔ Yán
translations.idiomatic: Lady Du, wife of Xu Yan

sentences.zh: 許延妻杜氏，不知何許人也。

translations.literal: Lady Dù, wife of Xǔ Yán, was of unknown origin.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yan's wife Lady Du—her home is unrecorded.

sentences.zh: 延為益州別駕，為李驤所害。

translations.literal: Yán served as Provincial Aide in Yizhou when Li Xiāng murdered him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiang killed him while he served as Yizhou aide.

sentences.zh: 驤欲納杜氏為妻，杜氏號哭守夫屍，罵驤曰：「汝輩逆賊無道，死有先後，寧當久活！

translations.literal: Xiāng wished to take Lady Dù as wife; she wailed beside her husband's corpse and cursed Xiāng: "You rebels lack every decency—death comes soon or late; would I cling to life!
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiang meant to marry her; she clung to her husband's body and howled that rebels like him died in due course—she would not cling to breath.

sentences.zh: 我杜家女，豈為賊妻也！

translations.literal: I am a daughter of the Du clan—how could I become a bandit's wife!
translations.idiomatic: A Du woman would never wed a traitor!

sentences.zh: 」驤怒，遂害之。

translations.literal: Enraged, Xiāng killed her.
translations.idiomatic: Furious, Li Xiang cut her down.

sentences.zh: 虞潭母孫氏

translations.literal: Lady Sūn, mother of Yú Tán
translations.idiomatic: Lady Sun, mother of Yu Tan

sentences.zh: 虞潭母孫氏，吳郡富春人，孫權族孫女也。

translations.literal: The mother of Yú Tán, née Sūn, was a native of Fuchun in Wujun and a grand-niece of Sun Quan by clan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Tan's mother, Lady Sun of Fuchun in Wu commandery, belonged to Sun Quan's lineage.

sentences.zh: 初適潭父忠，恭順貞和，甚有婦德。

translations.literal: When first married to Tán's father Zhōng, she was deferential, chaste, and harmonious, richly endowed with wifely virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Married to Tan's father Zhong, she was gentle, faithful, and harmonious—the model wife.

sentences.zh: 及忠亡，遺孤藐爾，孫氏雖少，誓不改節，躬自撫養，劬勞備至。

translations.literal: After Zhōng died he left a helpless orphan; though Lady Sūn was young she swore never to remarry, personally raising the child with utter devotion.
translations.idiomatic: Widowed young with a tiny son, she refused remarriage and raised him herself through every hardship.

sentences.zh: 性聰敏，識鑒過人。

translations.literal: By nature clever and keen, her discernment surpassed others.
translations.idiomatic: She was brilliant and saw farther than most.

sentences.zh: 潭始自幼童，便訓以忠義，故得聲望允洽，為朝廷所稱。

translations.literal: From boyhood she drilled Tán in loyalty and righteousness, so he earned the acclaim of the court.
translations.idiomatic: She taught Tan loyalty and duty while he was still a child, winning him court renown.

sentences.zh: 永嘉末，潭為南康太守，值杜弢構逆，率眾討之。

translations.literal: At the close of the Yongjia era Tán was governor of Nankang when Du Tao rebelled; Tán led troops against him.
translations.idiomatic: Early in exile Jin, as Nankang governor he marched against Du Tao's rebellion.

sentences.zh: 孫氏勉潭以必死之義，俱傾其資產以饋戰士，潭遂克捷。

translations.literal: Lady Sūn urged him with the duty to face death without flinch and poured out her entire fortune to feed the soldiers; Tán won the victory.
translations.idiomatic: His mother demanded he prefer death to dishonor and spent her estate on supplies—Tan broke the rebels.

sentences.zh: 及蘇峻作亂，潭時守吳興，又假節征峻。

translations.literal: When Su Jun rose in revolt, Tán then held Wuxing and received credentials to campaign against Jun.
translations.idiomatic: When Su Jun struck, Tan defended Wuxing and took imperial warrant to strike him.

sentences.zh: 孫氏戒之曰：「吾聞忠臣出孝子之門，汝當捨生取義，勿以吾老為累也。

translations.literal: Lady Sūn admonished him, "I have heard that loyal ministers spring from filial homes—you must risk life for righteousness; do not count my old age a burden.
translations.idiomatic: She warned him: faithful sons come from dutiful mothers—die if duty demands; ignore her frailty.

sentences.zh: 」仍盡發其家僮，令隨潭助戰，貿其所服環珮以為軍資。

translations.literal: She then armed every household slave to follow Tán, sold her rings and jade to finance the army.
translations.idiomatic: She drafted family retainers for his column and pawned her jewelry for war funds.

sentences.zh: 于時會稽內史王舒遣子允之為督護，孫氏又謂潭曰：「王府君遣兒征，汝何為獨不？

translations.literal: At that time the interior governor of Kuaiji, Wang Shu, sent his son Yunzhi as commander; Lady Sūn again told Tán, "Prefect Wang dispatches his son—why do you alone hold back?
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shu of Kuaiji sent his son Yunzhi as colonel, she asked why Tan refused his own son.

sentences.zh: 」潭即以子楚為督護，與舒允之合勢。

translations.literal: Tán thereupon appointed his son Chǔ colonel to join forces with Shu's Yunzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Tan then named his son Chu colonel to coordinate with Wang Yunzhi.

sentences.zh: 其憂國之誠如此。

translations.literal: Such was her earnest concern for the state.
translations.idiomatic: Her patriotism ran that deep.

sentences.zh: 拜武昌侯太夫人，加金章紫綬。

translations.literal: She was invested Dowager of the Marquisate of Wuchang and awarded the gold seal on purple ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: The court titled her Dowager of Wuchang marquis with gold seal and purple ribbon.

sentences.zh: 潭立養堂于家，王導以下皆就拜謁。

translations.literal: Tán built a reception hall at home where Wang Dao and every notable came to bow.
translations.idiomatic: Tan built her a hall at home; Wang Dao and the elite lined up to pay respects.

sentences.zh: 咸和末卒，年九十五。

translations.literal: She died at the close of the Xianhe era at ninety-five.
translations.idiomatic: She died in Xianhe's last years at ninety-five.

sentences.zh: 成帝遣使弔祭，諡曰定夫人。

translations.literal: Emperor Cheng dispatched envoys to mourn and sacrifice, posthumously dubbing her Lady Ding.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Cheng sent condolences and styled her Lady Ding.

sentences.zh: 周顗母李氏

translations.literal: Lady Lǐ, mother of Zhōu Yǐ
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li Luoxiu, mother of Zhou Yi

sentences.zh: 周顗母李氏，字絡秀，汝南人也。

translations.literal: The mother of Zhōu Yǐ, née Lǐ, courtesy Luòxiù, came from Runan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yi's mother Lady Li Luoxiu of Runan.

sentences.zh: 少時在室，顗父浚為安東將軍，時嘗出獵，遇雨，過止絡秀之家。

translations.literal: While still unmarried she lived at home when Yǐ's father Jùn, General Who Pacifies the East, once rode out hunting, encountered rain, and halted at Luòxiù's residence.
translations.idiomatic: Still a maiden when Zhou Jun hunted through rain and sheltered at her house.

sentences.zh: 會其家父兄不在，絡秀聞浚至，與一婢於內宰豬羊，具數十人之饌，甚精辦而不聞人聲。

translations.literal: Her father and brothers being absent, Luòxiù heard Jùn had arrived and, with a single maid, slaughtered pigs and sheep inside and spread a feast for dozens—everything exquisite yet without clamor.
translations.idiomatic: Her brothers gone, she secretly butchered livestock and laid out a feast for dozens without a sound.

sentences.zh: 浚怪使覘之，獨見一女子甚美，浚因求為妾。

translations.literal: Jùn wondered and sent someone to spy; he alone saw an exceedingly beautiful girl and therefore sought her as concubine.
translations.idiomatic: Jun peeked in, saw only a stunning girl, and asked for her as concubine.

sentences.zh: 其父兄不許，絡秀曰：「門戶殄瘁，何惜一女！

translations.literal: Her father and brothers refused; Luòxiù said, "Our house is ruined—why cling to one daughter!
translations.idiomatic: Her kin refused; she argued the clan was shattered—why spare one girl?

sentences.zh: 若連姻貴族，將來庶有大益矣。

translations.literal: If we ally with a noble house, future profit may be immense.
translations.idiomatic: An alliance with honor might yet restore them.

sentences.zh: 」父兄許之。

translations.literal: Father and brothers consented.
translations.idiomatic: They relented.

sentences.zh: 遂生顗及嵩、謨。

translations.literal: She then bore Yǐ as well as Song and Mo.
translations.idiomatic: She bore Zhou Yi, Zhou Song, and Zhou Mo.

sentences.zh: 而顗等既長，絡秀謂之曰：「我屈節為汝家作妾，門戶計耳。

translations.literal: When Yǐ and the others had grown, Luòxiù told them, "I humbled myself to become your family's concubine for the sake of our gate alone.
translations.idiomatic: When they matured she reminded them she became a concubine solely to lift the Li clan.

sentences.zh: 汝不與我家為親親者，吾亦何惜餘年！

translations.literal: If you will not treat my kin as true relatives, why should I cherish what years remain!
translations.idiomatic: If they spurned her family, she would disown them in turn.

sentences.zh: 」顗等從命，由此李氏遂得為方雅之族。

translations.literal: Yǐ and the rest obeyed; the Li family thereby joined the ranks of refined houses.
translations.idiomatic: They complied, and the Lis entered polite society.

sentences.zh: 中興時，顗等並列顯位。

translations.literal: At court's restoration Yǐ and his brothers all rose to high office.
translations.idiomatic: After the court crossed south they each climbed to rank.

sentences.zh: 嘗冬至置酒，絡秀舉觴賜三子曰：「吾本渡江，托足無所，不謂爾等並貴，列吾目前，吾復何憂！

translations.literal: Once at the winter solstice she set wine and raised a cup to her three sons: "When we fled south I had nowhere to stand—I never dreamed you would all become great officers arrayed before me; what more could I worry over!
translations.idiomatic: At a winter banquet she toasted her sons: refugees once footloose, now three dignitaries faced her—what grief remained?

sentences.zh: 」高起曰：「恐不如尊旨。

translations.literal: Song rose and replied, "We fear it may not match your intent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Song stood and warned that her joy might be premature.

sentences.zh: 伯仁志大而才短，名重而識暗，好乘人之弊，此非自全之道。

translations.literal: Bórén's ambitions exceed his talents; his fame outruns his judgment; he loves exploiting others' faults—that is no way to preserve oneself.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yi aimed too high for his gifts—renowned yet blind—always exploiting cracks in others—no recipe for safety.

sentences.zh: 嵩性抗直，亦不容於世。

translations.literal: Song's nature is blunt and upright—likewise the world will not tolerate him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Song's blunt pride would earn the world's spite.

sentences.zh: 唯阿奴碌碌，當在阿母目下耳。

translations.literal: Only little Ānü plods along—he will remain beneath his mother's eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Only little A'nu would stay ordinary under her eye.

sentences.zh: 」阿奴，謨小字也。

translations.literal: Ānü is the childhood name of Mo.
translations.idiomatic: A'nu was Zhou Mo's pet name.

sentences.zh: 後果如其言。

translations.literal: Later events proved exactly as she said.
translations.idiomatic: Events proved her right.

sentences.zh: 張茂妻陸氏

translations.literal: Lady Lù, wife of Zhāng Mào
translations.idiomatic: Lady Lu, wife of Zhang Mao

sentences.zh: 張茂妻陸氏，吳郡人也。

translations.literal: The wife of Zhāng Mào, née Lù, came from Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mao's wife Lady Lu of Wu.

sentences.zh: 茂為吳郡太守，被沈充所害，陸氏傾家產，率茂部曲為先登以討充。

translations.literal: Mào was governor of Wu commandery when Shen Chong murdered him; Lady Lù poured out her household fortune and led Mao's private troops as vanguard to attack Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Chong killed Governor Zhang Mao; Lady Lu spent her estate and led his bodyguard vanguard against Shen.

sentences.zh: 充敗，陸詣闕上書，為茂謝不克之責。

translations.literal: When Chong was defeated, Lady Lù went to the palace gate with a memorial apologizing for Mao's failure to defeat the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: After Shen's defeat she petitioned the throne, begging forgiveness for Mao's defeat.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「茂夫妻忠誠，舉門義烈，宜追贈茂太僕。」

translations.literal: An edict responded: "Mào and his wife were loyal and sincere; the entire household displayed righteous valor—Mào should be posthumously honored as Grand Coachman."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied that the Zhangs had been loyal—posthumously promote Mao to Grand Coachman.

sentences.zh: 尹虞二女

translations.literal: The two daughters of Yǐn Yú
translations.idiomatic: The two daughters of Yin Yu

sentences.zh: 尹虞二女，長沙人也。

translations.literal: The two daughters of Yǐn Yú were natives of Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Yu's daughters were Changsha women.

sentences.zh: 虞前任始興太守，起兵討杜弢，戰敗，二女為弢所獲，並有國色，弢將妻之。

translations.literal: Yú had previously been prefect of Shixing; he raised troops against Du Tao, was defeated, and his two daughters fell into Tao's hands—both were nationally lovely, and Tao's officers wished to marry them.
translations.idiomatic: Former Shixing prefect Yin Yu fell to Du Tao; his stunning daughters were captured—bandits meant to wed them.

sentences.zh: 女曰：「我父二千石，終不能為賊婦，有死而已！

translations.literal: The girls said, "Our father was a two-thousand-dan official—we will never be bandit wives; death alone awaits us!
translations.idiomatic: They shouted that their father held two-thousand-dan rank—they would die before wedding rebels.

sentences.zh: 」弢並害之。

translations.literal: Tao murdered them both.
translations.idiomatic: Du Tao executed both.

sentences.zh: 荀崧小女灌

translations.literal: Guàn, youngest daughter of Xún Sōng
translations.idiomatic: Xun Guan, youngest daughter of Xun Song

sentences.zh: 荀崧小女灌，幼有奇節。

translations.literal: Guàn, youngest daughter of Xún Sōng, showed singular integrity even in childhood.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Song's daughter Guan was a prodigy of resolve.

sentences.zh: 崧為襄城太守，為杜曾所圍，力弱食盡，欲求救于故吏平南將軍石覽，計無從出。

translations.literal: Sōng was governor of Xiangcheng when besieged by Du Zeng; strength failed and food ran out—he wished to beg relief from his former subordinate the General Who Pacifies the South, Shi Lan, yet saw no path.
translations.idiomatic: Du Zeng besieged Xun Song at Xiangcheng until supplies vanished; he needed Shi Lan's relief but had no messenger.

sentences.zh: 灌時年十三，乃率勇士數千人，逾城突圍夜出。

translations.literal: Guan was thirteen when she led several thousand picked warriors over the walls by night to break the ring.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen she led thousands in a night sortie over the wall.

sentences.zh: 賊追甚急，灌督厲將士，且戰且前，得入魯陽山獲免。

translations.literal: The enemy pressed hard; Guan rallied officers to fight while advancing until they reached Mount Luyang and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Pursued fiercely, she fought through to Luyang Mountain and broke free.

sentences.zh: 自詣覽乞師，又為崧書與南中郎將周訪請援，仍結為兄弟，訪即遣子撫率三千人會石覽俱救崧。

translations.literal: She personally sought Lan for troops, drafted a letter for Song to the General of the Center Army Zhou Fang requesting aid, swore brotherhood with Fang, and Fang immediately sent his son Fu with three thousand men to join Shi Lan in relieving Song.
translations.idiomatic: She begged Shi Lan for soldiers, wrote Zhou Fang for reinforcements, bonded with him as a sworn brother, and Zhou Fang sent three thousand men under his son Fu alongside Shi Lan to lift the siege.

sentences.zh: 賊聞兵至，散走，灌之力也。

translations.literal: When the rebels heard troops had arrived they scattered and fled—it was thanks to Guan's efforts.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits fled at the approach of relief forces—credit belonged to Xun Guan's valor.

sentences.zh: 王凝之妻謝道韞

translations.literal: Xiè Dàoyùn, wife of Wang Níngzhī
translations.idiomatic: Xie Daoyun, wife of Wang Ningzhi

sentences.zh: 王凝之妻謝氏，字道韞，安西將軍奕之女也。

translations.literal: The wife of Wang Níngzhī, née Xiè, courtesy Dàoyùn, was the daughter of General Who Pacifies the West Xiè Yì.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ningzhi's wife Lady Xie Daoyun was daughter of Xie Yi, general pacifying the west.

sentences.zh: 聰識有才辯。

translations.literal: She was perceptive, intelligent, and eloquent.
translations.idiomatic: Bright, insightful, and sharp in debate.

sentences.zh: 叔父安嘗問：「《毛詩》何句最佳？

translations.literal: Her uncle Àn once asked, "Which line of the Mao edition of the Classic of Poetry is finest?"
translations.idiomatic: Uncle Xie An asked which Mao Poetry couplet she liked best.

sentences.zh: 」道韞稱：「吉甫作頌，穆如清風。

translations.literal: Dàoyùn cited: "Jífǔ composed the hymn—grave as a cleansing breeze.
translations.idiomatic: She answered with the ode: "Jifu's hymn comes mild as clear wind."

sentences.zh: 仲山甫永懷，以慰其心。

translations.literal: Zhòng Shānfǔ ever cherishes—thus comforting his heart."
translations.idiomatic: "Zhong Shanfu holds fast in longing—easing the royal mind."

sentences.zh: 」安謂有雅人深致。

translations.literal: Àn pronounced this the insight of a refined spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Xie An called it the taste of a true aesthete.

sentences.zh: 又嘗內集，俄而雪驟下，安曰：「何所似也？

translations.literal: Again the family gathered within doors when suddenly snow drove down; Àn asked, "What does this resemble?"
translations.idiomatic: Once during an indoor gathering snow burst forth; Xie An asked what it resembled.

sentences.zh: 」安兄子朗曰：「散鹽空中差可擬。

translations.literal: Àn's nephew Lǎng answered, "Scattering salt through the air might compare.
translations.idiomatic: Nephew Xie Lang said scattered salt was the nearest likeness.

sentences.zh: 」道韞曰：「未若柳絮因風起。

translations.literal: Dàoyùn said, "Better still are willow catkins lifted on the wind."
translations.idiomatic: Daoyun answered that willow floss riding the gust suited better.

sentences.zh: 」安大悅。

translations.literal: Àn was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Xie An beamed with pride.

sentences.zh: 初適凝之，還，甚不樂。

translations.literal: When first married to Níngzhī she returned home deeply unhappy.
translations.idiomatic: She came home glum after marrying Wang Ningzhi.

sentences.zh: 安曰：「王郎，逸少子，不惡，汝何恨也？

translations.literal: Àn said, "Lord Wang is the son of Yìshào—hardly a poor match—why resent him?"
translations.idiomatic: Her uncle protested: Wang was Xie Xuan's distinguished son—why sulk?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「一門叔父則有阿大、中郎，群從兄弟復有封、胡、羯、末，不意天壤之中乃有王郎！

translations.literal: She replied, "Among house uncles we have Elder and Middle Uncle; among cousins again Fēng, Hú, Jié, and Mò—to think heaven and earth could hold such a Lord Wang!"
translations.idiomatic: She answered that between uncles like Xie Shang and cousins nicknamed Feng, Hu, Jie, and Mo, she never dreamed the world could harbor Wang Ningzhi.

sentences.zh: 」封謂謝韶，胡謂謝朗，羯謂謝玄，末謂謝川，皆其小字也。

translations.literal: Fēng denotes Xiè Sháo, Hú denotes Xiè Lǎng, Jié denotes Xiè Xuán, Mò denotes Xiè Chuān—all childhood names.
translations.idiomatic: Feng was Xie Shao, Hu Xie Lang, Jie Xie Xuan, Mo Xie Chuan—family pet names.

sentences.zh: 又嘗譏玄學植不進，曰：「為塵務經心，為天分有限邪？

translations.literal: She also ridiculed Xuán for slack scholarship: "Are worldly cares blocking you, or is native talent simply bounded?"
translations.idiomatic: She needled Xie Xuan's slow progress—was dust-clogged duty to blame or shallow genius?

sentences.zh: 」凝之弟獻之嘗與賓客談議，詞理將屈，道韞遣婢白獻之曰：「欲為小郎解圍。

translations.literal: Níngzhī's younger brother Xiànzhī once debated guests until logic faltered; Dàoyùn sent a maid to tell Xiànzhī, "Your sister-in-law wishes to relieve the young lord's embarrassment.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Xianzhi floundered before visitors, she offered through a maid to lift him from the trap.

sentences.zh: 」乃施青綾步鄣自蔽，申獻之前議，客不能屈。

translations.literal: She then deployed a blue silk screen to shield herself, clarified Xiànzhī's earlier argument, and the guests could not overcome her.
translations.idiomatic: Behind an azure screen she picked up his thread and routed every objection.

sentences.zh: 及遭孫恩之難，舉厝自若，既聞夫及諸子已為賊所害，方命婢肩輿抽刃出門。

translations.literal: When calamity struck from Sun Ēn she remained composed; learning husband and sons had already fallen to bandits, she ordered maids to shoulder her litter and bore blades through the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Sun En's rebellion left her calm until word came that Wang Ningzhi and her sons were dead—then she rode out in a sedan, blades ready.

sentences.zh: 亂兵稍至，手殺數人，乃被虜。

translations.literal: As disorderly troops closed in she slew several with her own hands before capture.
translations.idiomatic: She killed several soldiers herself before they seized her.

sentences.zh: 其外孫劉濤時年數歲，賊又欲害之，道韞曰：「事在王門，何關他族！

translations.literal: Her grandson Liú Tāo was still a few years old when bandits meant to kill him too; Dàoyùn cried, "The affair rests with the Wang clan—what business have outsiders here!
translations.idiomatic: When brigands threatened toddler grandson Liu Tao, she insisted his fate belonged to the Wang family alone—leave other houses aside.

sentences.zh: 必其如此，寧先見殺。

translations.literal: If it must come to this, I would sooner die first.
translations.idiomatic: If they insisted on blood, let them strike her down before the boy.

sentences.zh: 」恩雖毒虐，為之改容，乃不害濤。

translations.literal: Though Ēn was vicious cruelty itself, her words softened him and he spared Tāo.
translations.idiomatic: Even ruthless Sun En relented and let the boy live.

sentences.zh: 自爾嫠居會稽，家中莫不嚴肅。

translations.literal: Thereafter widowed in Kuaiji, none in her household dared lax discipline.
translations.idiomatic: As widow in Kuaiji she ruled the clan with iron dignity.

sentences.zh: 太守劉柳聞其名，請與談議。

translations.literal: Prefect Liǔ Liǔ heard her fame and requested conversation.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Liu Liu sought an audience after hearing of her.

sentences.zh: 道韞素知柳名，亦不自阻，乃簪髻素褥坐於帳中，柳束脩整帶造於別榻。

translations.literal: Dàoyùn knew Liǔ's reputation and did not shrink away; pinning hair and seated on plain mat inside a curtain, Liǔ tied sash and approached another couch.
translations.idiomatic: She knew Liu Liu's name, pinned her hair, sat on white felt behind drapes; Liu tidied his sash on a separate seat.

sentences.zh: 道韞風韻高邁，敘致清雅，先及家事，慷慨流漣，徐酬問旨，詞理無滯。

translations.literal: Her bearing towered above the ordinary; narrative tone stayed lucid as spring water—she opened with household cares, passion surging, then answered questions slowly with flawless reasoning.
translations.idiomatic: Her manner was lofty, her storytelling lucid—she began with family sorrow, then fielded questions without stumbling.

sentences.zh: 柳退而歎曰：「實頃所未見，瞻察言氣，使人心形俱服。

translations.literal: Liǔ withdrew sighing, "Never in years have I seen the like—tone and bearing alike command utter submission.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Liu left marveling that voice and spirit alike humbled him.

sentences.zh: 」道韞亦云：「親從凋亡，始遇此士，聽其所問，殊開人胸府。」

translations.literal: Dàoyùn likewise said, "With kin fallen away I meet this gentleman at last—his questions opened vistas I had never glimpsed."
translations.idiomatic: Daoyun added that after bereavement Liu Liu's inquiry awakened whole new thoughts.

sentences.zh: 初，同郡張玄妹亦有才質，適於顧氏，玄每稱之，以敵道韞。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhāng Xuán's younger sister in the same commandery also possessed talent and married into the Gù clan; Xuán constantly praised her as rivaling Dàoyùn.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xuan boasted his talented sister married to the Gus matched Daoyun.

sentences.zh: 有濟尼者，游於二家，或問之，濟尼答曰：「王夫人神情散朗，故有林下風氣。

translations.literal: A nun named Jì wandered both households; asked to compare them she answered, "Lady Wang's spirit roams open and bright—she bears the temper of the bamboo grove.
translations.idiomatic: Nun Ji visited both homes and said Lady Wang had reclusive scholars' breeze.

sentences.zh: 顧家婦清心玉映，自是閨房之秀。

translations.literal: The Gu daughter-in-law holds a heart pure as jade reflecting light—naturally the pearl of the women's quarters.
translations.idiomatic: The Gu bride shone with icy clarity—the inner chambers' finest jewel.

sentences.zh: 」道韞所著詩賦誄頌並傳於世。

translations.literal: The poems, fu, dirges, and hymns authored by Dàoyùn circulate in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyun's verse and prose survived her age.

sentences.zh: 劉臻妻陳氏

translations.literal: Lady Chén, wife of Liú Zhēn
translations.idiomatic: Lady Chen, wife of Liu Zhen

sentences.zh: 劉臻妻陳氏者，亦聰辯能屬文。

translations.literal: Lady Chén, wife of Liú Zhēn, was likewise clever in debate and could compose texts.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhen's wife Lady Chen was eloquent and literary.

sentences.zh: 嘗正旦獻《椒花頌》，其詞曰：「旋穹周回，三朝肇建。

translations.literal: On New Year's morning she presented an "Ode to Pepper Blossoms"; its words run: "The revolving vault circles round—the triple dawn begins.
translations.idiomatic: Her New Year's Pepper Blossom Ode begins: "The dome of heaven wheels—three courts inaugurate the year."

sentences.zh: 青陽散輝，澄景載煥。

translations.literal: Green spring spreads radiance; limpid sunlight gleams anew.
translations.idiomatic: Spring sunlight spreads; clear beams renew the scene.

sentences.zh: 標美靈葩，爰采爰獻。

translations.literal: We mark the sacred blossom—pluck it and offer it up.
translations.idiomatic: They praise the auspicious bloom—gather and present it.

sentences.zh: 聖容映之，永壽于萬。

translations.literal: The sage countenance mirrored here—may ten thousand years bless him forever."
translations.idiomatic: Sacred face reflected—may myriad years grace the throne."

sentences.zh: 」又撰元日及冬至進見之儀，行於世。

translations.literal: She also drafted audience etiquette for New Year's Day and winter solstice that circulated in society.
translations.idiomatic: She codified New Year and solstice court rituals that became standard usage.

sentences.zh: 皮京妻龍憐

translations.literal: Lóng Lián, wife of Pí Jīng
translations.idiomatic: Long Lian, wife of Pi Jing

sentences.zh: 皮京妻龍氏，字憐，西道縣人也。

translations.literal: The wife of Pí Jīng, née Lóng, courtesy Lián, came from Xidao county.
translations.idiomatic: Pi Jing's wife Lady Long Lian hailed from Xidao county.

sentences.zh: 年十三適京，未逾年而京卒，京二弟亦相次而隕，既無胤嗣，又無期功之親。

translations.literal: At thirteen she married Jīng; before a year passed Jīng died, and both younger brothers likewise fell in succession—there were neither heirs nor even mourners within nine ritual grades.
translations.idiomatic: She wed at thirteen; Pi Jing died within the year, then both his brothers—no offspring, no close kin to mourn.

sentences.zh: 憐貨其嫁時資裝，躬自紡織，數年間三喪俱舉，葬斂既畢，每時享祭無闕。

translations.literal: Lián sold her trousseau goods and spun cloth herself; within several years she observed all three funerals; once burial closed she never missed seasonal sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: She pawned her dowry, wove for coin, buried three coffins, then kept every memorial feast.

sentences.zh: 州裏聞其賢，屢有娉者，憐誓不改醮，守節窮居五十餘載而卒。

translations.literal: The district praised her virtue; suitors came repeatedly, yet Lián swore never to remarry, guarding her widowhood more than fifty years until death.
translations.idiomatic: Neighbors admired her; matchmakers kept calling, but she stayed chaste five decades.

sentences.zh: 孟昶妻周氏

translations.literal: Lady Zhōu, wife of Mèng Chǎng
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhou, wife of Meng Chang

sentences.zh: 孟昶妻周氏，昶弟顗妻又其從妹也。

translations.literal: The wife of Mèng Chǎng, Lady Zhōu, was likewise cousin to the wife of Chǎng's brother Yǐ.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Chang's wife Lady Zhou was cousin to Meng Yi's wife.

sentences.zh: 二家並豐財產。

translations.literal: Both households possessed abundant wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Both families were immensely rich.

sentences.zh: 初，桓玄雅重昶而劉邁毀之，昶知，深自惋失。

translations.literal: At first Huán Xuān esteemed Chǎng while Liú Mài slandered him; Chǎng learned of it and nursed deep regret.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan favored Meng Chang until Liu Mai smeared him—Chang stewed in resentment.

sentences.zh: 及劉裕將建義，與昶定謀，昶欲盡散財物以供軍糧，其妻非常婦人，可語以大事，乃謂之曰：「劉邁毀我於桓公，便是一生淪陷，決當作賊。

translations.literal: When Liú Yù prepared to raise righteous arms and plotted with Chǎng, Chǎng wished to disburse every asset for army grain; his wife was no ordinary woman—fit to share great affairs—so he told her, "Liú Mài ruined me before Huán Xuān—I am ruined for life and must rebel.
translations.idiomatic: As Liu Yu plotted revolt, Meng Chang meant to spend his fortune on supplies; he told his wife Liu Mai had doomed him with Huan Xuan—only rebellion remained.

sentences.zh: 卿幸可早爾離絕，脫得富貴，相迎不晚也。

translations.literal: Divorce me quickly while you may; should fortune smile we can reunite later.
translations.idiomatic: Better separate now; they could reunite after victory.

sentences.zh: 」周氏曰：「君父母在堂，欲建非常之謀，豈婦人所諫！

translations.literal: Lady Zhōu replied, "Your parents yet live—you contemplate extraordinary schemes—should a woman protest!
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhou shot back that parents still lived—counsel could not stop him.

sentences.zh: 事之不成，當于奚官中奉養大家，義無歸志也。

translations.literal: Should the venture fail I shall tend them among palace servants—I will never think of returning home.
translations.idiomatic: If he failed she would slave in the palace kitchens before forsaking in-laws.

sentences.zh: 」昶愴然久之而起。

translations.literal: Chǎng mourned silently long before rising.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Chang rose grimly after brooding.

sentences.zh: 周氏追昶坐，云：「觀君舉厝，非謀及婦人者，不過欲得財物耳。

translations.literal: Lady Zhōu pulled him to sit, saying, "Judging your manner you never meant to consult a wife—you only crave funds.
translations.idiomatic: She tugged him down: his scheme was plainly about money, not counsel.

sentences.zh: 」時其所生女在抱，推而示之曰：「此而可賣，亦當不惜，況資財乎！

translations.literal: Her infant daughter lay in her arms; thrusting the child forward she said, "If this girl may be sold I would not cling to her—how much less mere treasure!
translations.idiomatic: She held their baby—sell the child if needed, let alone coin.

sentences.zh: 」遂傾資產以給之，而托以他用。

translations.literal: She therefore emptied their wealth to supply him while pretending other uses.
translations.idiomatic: She handed over their fortune under cover of ordinary errands.

sentences.zh: 及事之將舉，周氏謂顗妻云：「一昨夢殊不好，門內宜浣濯沐浴以除之，且不宜赤色，我當悉取作七日藏厭。

translations.literal: As action neared Lady Zhōu told Yǐ's wife, "Yesterday's dream was ominous—the household should wash and bathe to cleanse it, and avoid red garments—I shall collect every scarlet piece for a seven-day apotropaic seclusion.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of the coup she warned Meng Yi's wife of bad dreams—demanding red cloth for a week-long ritual cleanse.

sentences.zh: 」顗妻信之，所有絳色者悉斂以付焉。

translations.literal: Yǐ's wife trusted her and surrendered every crimson garment.
translations.idiomatic: The cousin wife surrendered all red silk.

sentences.zh: 乃置帳中，潛自剔綿，以絳與昶，遂得數十人被服赫然，悉周氏所出，而家人不之知也。

translations.literal: Lady Zhōu hid them behind curtains, secretly frayed cotton stuffing, supplied crimson cloth to Chǎng, and thus armed dozens of men in blazing uniforms—all Zhou's doing though kin suspected nothing.
translations.idiomatic: She shredded lining in secret, fed scarlet cloth to Meng Chang, and clothed dozens of warriors—kin never guessed.

sentences.zh: 何無忌母劉氏

translations.literal: Lady Liú, mother of Hé Wújì
translations.idiomatic: Lady Liu, mother of He Wuji

sentences.zh: 何無忌母劉氏，征虜將軍建之女也。

translations.literal: The mother of Hé Wújì, Lady Liú, was daughter of General Who Conquers Captives Liú Jiàn.
translations.idiomatic: He Wuji's mother Lady Liu was daughter of Liu Jian, conqueror general.

sentences.zh: 少有志節。

translations.literal: From youth she possessed stalwart resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Even young she had backbone.

sentences.zh: 弟牢之為桓玄所害，劉氏每銜之，常思報復。

translations.literal: Her younger brother Láozhī fell to Huán Xuān's hand; Lady Liú nursed constant hatred and plotted revenge.
translations.idiomatic: Brother Liu Laozhi died at Huan Xuan's order—she burned for vengeance.

sentences.zh: 及無忌與劉裕定謀，而劉氏察其舉厝有異，喜而不言。

translations.literal: When Wújì allied with Liú Yù in conspiracy Lady Liú detected his altered bearing and rejoiced yet stayed silent.
translations.idiomatic: She noticed He Wuji's restless plotting with Liu Yu and smiled inwardly.

sentences.zh: 會無忌夜于屏風裹制檄文，劉氏潛以器覆燭，徐登橙于屏風上窺之，既知，泣而撫之曰：「我不如東海呂母明矣！

translations.literal: Once Wújì drafted a proclamation behind a folding screen by night; Lady Liú quietly covered the candle with a vessel, climbed a stool to peek above the screen, and learning the truth wept while embracing him: "I cannot match Mother Lǚ of Donghai for clarity!
translations.idiomatic: Spying him compose a coup manifesto behind screens, she smothered the candle, climbed a stool, read his plot, and wept—thrilled he would eclipse Donghai's Lady Lü.

sentences.zh: 既孤其誠，常恐壽促，汝能如此，吾仇恥雪矣。

translations.literal: Solitary devotion such as mine ever feared short life—now you act thus and my shame is avenged.
translations.idiomatic: Lonely vigil had haunted her; now her vendetta could clear.

sentences.zh: 」因問其同謀，知事在裕，彌喜，乃說桓玄必敗、義師必成之理以勸勉之。

translations.literal: She asked his fellow plotters; learning Liu Yu led them she rejoiced the more, explaining why Huán Xuān must fall and the righteous army prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Learning Liu Yu commanded the plot she lectured him on Huan Xuan's doom.

sentences.zh: 後果如其言。

translations.literal: Later events matched her words.
translations.idiomatic: History proved her right.

sentences.zh: 劉聰妻劉娥

translations.literal: Lady Liú È, wife of Liú Cōng
translations.idiomatic: Liu E, consort of Liu Cong (Han-Zhao)

sentences.zh: 劉聰妻劉氏，名娥，字麗華，偽太保殷女也。

translations.literal: The wife of Liú Cōng, Lady Liú, named È, courtesy Lìhuá, was daughter of the Former Zhao Grand Guardian Yīn.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong's consort Liu E, courtesy Lihua, was daughter of minister Yin.

sentences.zh: 幼而聰慧，晝營女工，夜誦書籍，傅母恆止之，娥敦習彌厲。

translations.literal: Clever from childhood, she pursued women's work by day and read texts by night; nursing maids always stopped her, yet È studied all the harder.
translations.idiomatic: She sewed by day, read by night; nurses scolded her into deeper study.

sentences.zh: 每與諸兄論經義，理趣超遠，諸兄深以歎伏。

translations.literal: Whenever debating classics with elder brothers her reasoning soared; they marveled and conceded.
translations.idiomatic: Debating scripture with brothers she left them speechless.

sentences.zh: 性孝友，善風儀進止。

translations.literal: Filial, gentle, graceful in bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Loving, modest, poised.

sentences.zh: 聰既僭位，召為右貴嬪，甚寵之。

translations.literal: Once Cōng usurped the throne he summoned her as Noble Consort of the Right and favored her greatly.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Cong seized power he took her as senior consort and doted on her.

sentences.zh: 俄拜為后，將起䳨儀殿以居之，其廷尉陳元達切諫，聰大怒，將斬之。

translations.literal: Soon she became empress; he planned to erect the Yanyi Palace Hall for her dwelling—Court Administrator Chén Yuándá remonstrated bluntly; Cōng raged and meant to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: He promoted her to empress and broke ground on Yanyi Hall—Chen Yuanda's blunt protest nearly cost his head.

sentences.zh: 娥時在後堂，私敕左右停刑，手疏啟曰：「伏聞將為妾營殿，今昭德足居，䳨儀非急。

translations.literal: È stood in the rear hall and secretly ordered attendants to halt the execution; she drafted a memorial: "I hear Your Majesty builds me a palace—present virtue suffices for dwelling; Yanyi is no urgent need.
translations.idiomatic: From the rear quarters she stayed the blade and memorialized that Zhao-de Hall already housed her—Yanyi could wait.

sentences.zh: 四海未一，禍難猶繁，動須人力資財，尤宜慎之。

translations.literal: The realm is not united—calamity still swirls—every mobilization demands labor and treasure and demands utmost caution.
translations.idiomatic: The empire remained torn—every project burned treasure and lives.

sentences.zh: 廷尉之言，國家大政。

translations.literal: The Court Administrator speaks for the state's grand policy.
translations.idiomatic: The commandant addressed fundamental policy.

sentences.zh: 夫忠臣之諫，豈為身哉？

translations.literal: Does a loyal minister remonstrate for private gain?
translations.idiomatic: True ministers risk counsel for the throne, not themselves.

sentences.zh: 帝王距之，亦非顧身也。

translations.literal: When emperors reject advice they likewise seek no personal ease.
translations.idiomatic: Stubborn rulers refuse counsel for selfish ease.

sentences.zh: 妾仰謂陛下上尋明君納諫之昌，下忿暗主距諫之禍，宜賞廷尉以美爵，酬廷尉以列土，如何不惟不納，而反欲誅之？

translations.literal: I humbly reflect that wise sovereigns above prize accepting counsel; foolish rulers below treasure rejecting it—You should ennoble the Court Administrator, not raise sword against him—why reject honest words and aim to kill?
translations.idiomatic: She begged Liu Cong to honor wise rulers who welcomed advice and shun tyrants who spurned it—reward Chen Yuanda, do not kill him.

sentences.zh: 陛下此怒由妾而起，廷尉之禍由妾而招，人怨國疲，咎歸於妾，距諫害忠，亦妾之由。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's wrath stems from me; the Court Administrator's peril stems from me—popular resentment and national exhaustion trace to me; blocking counsel and harming loyalty likewise trace to me.
translations.idiomatic: She blamed herself for his rage, Chen's danger, and the realm's fatigue.

sentences.zh: 自古敗國喪家，未始不由婦人者也。

translations.literal: Since antiquity ruined states and lost houses began through women.
translations.idiomatic: Historically women undid dynasties.

sentences.zh: 妾每覽古事，忿之忘食，何意今日妾自為之！

translations.literal: Whenever I read ancient tales anger steals my meal—who imagined today I would become the example!
translations.idiomatic: Reading history she loathed such women—now she embodied them.

sentences.zh: 後人之觀妾，亦猶妾之視前人也，復何面目仰侍巾櫛，請歸死此堂，以塞陛下誤惑之過。

translations.literal: Posterity judging me will mirror my judgment of the past—what face remains to attend your toilette? I beg to die in this hall to answer Your Majesty's misguided passion.
translations.idiomatic: Future ages would condemn her as she condemned predecessors—she offered suicide to expiate his folly.

sentences.zh: 」聰覽之色變，謂其群下曰：「朕比得風疾，喜怒過常。

translations.literal: Cōng read it and changed color, telling ministers, "These days wind ailments skew my temper.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong blanched and blamed illness for his rage.

sentences.zh: 元達，忠臣也，朕甚愧之。

translations.literal: Yuándá is a loyal minister—I am deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yuanda was faithful—he felt shame.

sentences.zh: 」以娥表示元達曰：「外輔如公，內輔如此后，朕無憂矣。

translations.literal: He showed È's memorial to Yuándá: "With ministers such as you abroad and such an empress within I need not worry.
translations.idiomatic: He waved her plea before Chen: inner and outer pillars alike steadied him.

sentences.zh: 」及娥死，偽諡武宣皇后。

translations.literal: After È died she received posthumous title Empress Wuxuan of Former Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu E died Han Zhao styled her Empress Wuxuan.

sentences.zh: 其姊英，字麗芳，亦聰敏涉學，而文詞機辯，曉達政事，過於娥。

translations.literal: Her elder sister Yīng, courtesy Lìfāng, was likewise acute, versed in letters, rhetoric, and statecraft—surpassing È.
translations.idiomatic: Sister Liu Ying, courtesy Lifang, surpassed her in wit and policy debate.

sentences.zh: 初與娥同召拜左貴嬪，尋卒，偽追諡武德皇后。

translations.literal: Initially summoned with È as Noble Consort of the Left she soon died and received posthumous Empress Wude.
translations.idiomatic: She entered together as left consort but died young—posthumously Empress Wude.

sentences.zh: 王廣女

translations.literal: The daughter of Wang Guǎng
translations.idiomatic: The daughter of Wang Guang

sentences.zh: 王廣女者，不知何許人也。

translations.literal: The daughter of Wang Guǎng was of unknown origin.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guang's daughter—her homeland unknown.

sentences.zh: 容質甚美，慷慨有丈夫之節。

translations.literal: Lovely in appearance, passionate and possessed of masculine resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Stunning and fiercely courageous.

sentences.zh: 廣仕劉聰，為西揚州刺史。

translations.literal: Guǎng served Liú Cōng as Inspector of West Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guang served Liu Cong as governor of western Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 蠻帥梅芳攻陷揚州，而廣被殺。

translations.literal: Barbarian commander Méi Fāng captured Yangzhou and slew Guǎng.
translations.idiomatic: Chieftain Mei Fang stormed Yangzhou and killed Wang Guang.

sentences.zh: 王時年十五，芳納之。

translations.literal: The Wang girl was fifteen when Fāng took her as concubine.
translations.idiomatic: Mei Fang seized fifteen-year-old Wang Guang as concubine.

sentences.zh: 俄於暗室擊芳，不中，芳驚起曰：「何故反邪？

translations.literal: Soon in a dark chamber she struck at Fāng and missed; Fāng started up demanding, "Why betray me?
translations.idiomatic: Soon she ambushed him in darkness—missed; Mei Fang cried treason.

sentences.zh: 」王罵曰：「蠻畜！

translations.literal: Wang cursed, "Barbarian beast!"
translations.idiomatic: She screamed, "Savage!"

sentences.zh: 我欲誅反賊，何謂反乎？

translations.literal: I mean to execute traitors—how am I the rebel?
translations.idiomatic: I strike rebels—how dare you call me traitor?

sentences.zh: 吾聞父仇不同天，母仇不同地，汝反逆無狀，害人父母，而復以無禮陵人，吾所以不死者，欲誅汝耳！

translations.literal: I have heard that father's foe cannot share heaven, mother's foe cannot share earth—you murderous invert without shame, destroying others' parents, then bullying me with insult—my reason for living was to slay you!
translations.idiomatic: Father's blood feud brooks no shared sky—Mei Fang slew her parents yet vaunts over her—she endured only to kill him.

sentences.zh: 今死自吾分，不待汝殺，但恨不得梟汝首於通逵，以塞大恥。

translations.literal: Now death is my allotted lot—I need not wait for your blade—only I regret that I cannot expose your head at the crossroads to answer this supreme shame.
translations.idiomatic: Death was hers already—she only regretted failing to spike his skull at the public crossing.

sentences.zh: 」辭氣猛厲，言終乃自殺，芳止之不可。

translations.literal: Her words rang fierce as steel; speech ended and she killed herself—Fang could not stop her.
translations.idiomatic: Voice like iron, she fell on her blade before Mei Fang could seize her.

sentences.zh: 陝婦人

translations.literal: The Woman of Shǎn
translations.idiomatic: The Woman of Shanzhou

sentences.zh: 陝婦人，不知姓字，年十九。

translations.literal: The woman of Shǎn—her surname and personal name are unknown; she was nineteen.
translations.idiomatic: A nineteen-year-old widow of Shan county—name lost.

sentences.zh: 劉曜時嫠居陝縣，事叔姑甚謹，其家欲嫁之，此婦毀面自誓。

translations.literal: Under Liu Yao she dwelt widowed in Shǎn county, serving her aunt with utmost care; her kin wished to remarry her, but she scarred her face and swore an oath.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao's reign found her widowed in Shan, dutiful to her aunt-in-law; kin pressed remarriage so she disfigured herself.

sentences.zh: 後叔姑病死，其叔姑有女在夫家，先從此婦乞假不得，因而誣殺其母，有司不能察而誅之。

translations.literal: Later her aunt died of illness; the aunt had a daughter married elsewhere who, refused a loan earlier by this woman, then falsely accused her of murdering her mother—officials failed to investigate and executed her.
translations.idiomatic: When the aunt died, a spiteful cousin framed her for matricide after a loan snub—magistrates executed her unjustly.

sentences.zh: 時有群鳥悲鳴屍上，其聲甚哀，盛夏暴屍十日，不腐，亦不為蟲獸所敗，其境乃經歲不雨。
