translations.literal: At that time flocks of birds mourned atop the corpse—their cries heartrending; high summer left the body exposed ten days without decay or harm from insects or beasts, and the district went a year without rain.
translations.idiomatic: Birds keened over her corpse; midsummer heat failed to rot her—no beast touched her—and drought gripped the land a year.

sentences.zh: 曜遣呼延謨為太守，既知其冤，乃斬此女，設少牢以祭其墓，諡曰孝烈貞婦，其日大雨。

translations.literal: Yao dispatched Hūyán Mó as prefect; once he grasped her injustice he executed that daughter, offered lesser beast sacrifice at her tomb, posthumously titled her Chaste Filial Martyr—and that day great rain fell.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Huyan Mo avenged her, executed the false accuser, sacrificed at her grave as Lady Xiaolie—and rain broke.

sentences.zh: 靳康女

translations.literal: The daughter of Jìn Kāng
translations.idiomatic: The daughter of Jin Kang

sentences.zh: 靳康女者，不知何許人也。

translations.literal: The daughter of Jìn Kāng was of unknown origin.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Kang's daughter—homeland unknown.

sentences.zh: 美姿容，有志操。

translations.literal: Lovely in bearing and steadfast in resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Beautiful and principled.

sentences.zh: 劉曜之誅靳氏，將納靳女為妾，靳曰：「陛下既滅其父母兄弟，復何用妾為！

translations.literal: When Liu Yao executed the Jìn clan he planned to take the Jìn daughter as concubine; she replied, "Your Majesty has already destroyed her parents and brothers—what use have you for a concubine!
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong meant to bed her after wiping out her clan; she asked why he needed a trophy concubine.

sentences.zh: 妾聞逆人之誅也，尚汙宮伐樹，而況其子女乎！

translations.literal: I have heard that punishing rebels extends even to sullying palaces and felling groves—how much more their sons and daughters!
translations.idiomatic: Even conquered rebels suffer palace pollution and ancestral groves cut—why spare enemy seed?

sentences.zh: 」因號泣請死，曜哀之，免康一子。

translations.literal: She therefore wailed and begged death; Yao pitied her and spared one son of Kāng.
translations.idiomatic: She sobbed for execution until Liu Yao relented and spared one Jin Kang heir.

sentences.zh: 韋逞母宋氏

translations.literal: Lady Sòng, mother of Wéi Chěng
translations.idiomatic: Lady Song, mother of Wei Cheng

sentences.zh: 韋逞母宋氏，不知何郡人也，家世以儒學稱。

translations.literal: Lady Sòng, mother of Wéi Chěng—her native commandery is unknown; her house was famed for Confucian scholarship.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Cheng's mother Lady Song—unknown prefecture, scholarly clan.

sentences.zh: 宋氏幼喪母，其父躬自養之。

translations.literal: Lady Sòng lost her mother young; her father personally reared her.
translations.idiomatic: Motherless girl raised by her father.

sentences.zh: 及長，授以《周官》音義，謂之曰：「吾家世學《周官》，傳業相繼，此又周以所制，經紀典誥，百官品物，備於此矣。

translations.literal: When grown he transmitted to her the phonological glosses for the Offices of Zhou, telling her, "Our house has studied the Offices of Zhou for generations in unbroken succession; moreover the Zhou kings authored this text—it arrays statutes and commands, ranks and ritual vessels—everything lies therein.
translations.idiomatic: He taught her Zhou ritual glosses: generations had guarded this Zhou king scripture covering governance and ritual.

sentences.zh: 吾今無男可傳，汝可受之，勿令經世。

translations.literal: I now lack sons to inherit—you must receive this teaching and never allow it to vanish from the world.
translations.idiomatic: With no sons he entrusted her to preserve the lineage's Zhou learning.

sentences.zh: 」屬天下喪亂，宋氏諷誦不輟。

translations.literal: Though the realm plunged into chaos Lady Sòng never ceased recitation.
translations.idiomatic: Through wars she kept chanting the classics.

sentences.zh: 其後為石季龍徙之于山東，宋氏與夫在徙中，推鹿車，背負父所授書，到冀州，依膠東富人程安壽，壽養護之。

translations.literal: Later Shí Jìlóng relocated her household to Shandong; Lady Sòng and her husband marched among deportees pushing a deer cart, bearing on her back the books her father gave; reaching Jì province they lodged with the wealthy Chéng Ānshòu of Jiāodong, who sheltered them.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu exiled them east; she carted her father's Zhou texts on her back until Cheng Anshou of Jiaodong harbored them.

sentences.zh: 逞時年小，宋氏晝則樵采，夜則教逞，然紡績無廢。

translations.literal: Chěng was still small; by day Lady Sòng gathered firewood, by night she instructed Chěng, yet never neglected spinning.
translations.idiomatic: She chopped fuel by day, tutored Wei Cheng by night, never skipping weaving.

sentences.zh: 壽每歎曰：「學家多士大夫，得無是乎！

translations.literal: Ānshòu often sighed, "How many scholar houses boast ministers yet lack such devotion!
translations.idiomatic: Cheng marveled that pedigreed scholars rarely matched her.

sentences.zh: 」逞遂學成名立，仕苻堅為太常。

translations.literal: Chěng thereupon completed his studies and rose to office, serving Fu Jiān as Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Cheng mastered learning, joined Fu Jian as Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 堅嘗幸其太學，問博士經典，乃憫禮樂遺闕。

translations.literal: Jiān once visited the Imperial Academy and questioned academicians on the classics, lamenting lost ritual and music.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian toured the academy, quizzed doctors, mourned broken ritual.

sentences.zh: 時博士盧壼對曰：「廢學既久，書傳零落，此年綴撰，正經粗集，唯周官禮注未有其師。

translations.literal: Academician Lú Kǎn replied, "Learning long abandoned—texts scattered—only lately compiled; orthodox classics roughly gathered—only the Zhou offices commentary lacks a teacher.
translations.idiomatic: Doctor Lu Kan reported that Zhou ritual commentary still lacked a qualified teacher.

sentences.zh: 窺見太常韋逞母宋氏世學家女，傳其父業，得周官音義，今年八十，視聽無闕，自非此母無可以傳授後生。

translations.literal: We note Minister Wéi Chěng's mother Lady Sòng is an inheriting scholar's daughter who preserves her father's craft with Zhou offices glosses—now eighty yet sight and hearing keen—save this matron none can instruct youth.
translations.idiomatic: Only Lady Song, eighty and sharp, could teach Rites of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 」於是就宋氏家立講堂，置生員百二十人，隔絳紗幔而受業，號宋氏為宣文君，賜侍婢十人。

translations.literal: Thereupon they erected a lecture hall at her home, enrolled one hundred twenty students, hung crimson gauze while she taught behind it, styled her Lady Xuānwén, and gifted ten serving maids.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian opened a crimson-screen lecture hall at her door with 120 students and titled her Lady Xuanwen.

sentences.zh: 周官學復行于世，時稱韋氏宋母焉。

translations.literal: Learning of the Offices of Zhou again circulated in the age—all styled her Mother Song of the Wéi clan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou offices scholarship revived; people called her Mother Song Wei.

sentences.zh: 張天錫妾閻氏、薛氏

translations.literal: Concubines Yán and Xuē of Zhāng Tiānxī
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yan and Lady Xue, concubines of Zhang Tianxi

sentences.zh: 張天錫妾閻氏、薛氏，並不知何許人也，咸有寵於天錫。

translations.literal: The concubines Yán and Xuē of Zhāng Tiānxī—both homelands unknown—equally enjoyed Tiānxī's favor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tianxi's favored concubines Yan and Xue—origins unknown.

sentences.zh: 天錫寢疾，謂之曰：「汝二人將何以報我？

translations.literal: Tiānxī lay gravely ill and told them, "How will you two repay me?
translations.idiomatic: Dying, Zhang Tianxi asked how they would repay his love.

sentences.zh: 吾死後，豈可為人妻乎！

translations.literal: After my death how could you become another man's wife!
translations.idiomatic: After his death they must never remarry.

sentences.zh: 」皆曰：「尊若不諱，妾請效死，供灑掃地下，誓無他志。

translations.literal: Both answered, "Should my lord pass we beg to follow you in death, sweeping your tomb below ground—we swear no other intent.
translations.idiomatic: They vowed to die with him and sweep his tomb below.

sentences.zh: 」及其疾篤，二姬皆自刎。

translations.literal: When his illness turned critical both concubines cut their throats.
translations.idiomatic: As he sank both slit their throats.

sentences.zh: 天錫疾瘳，追悼之，以夫人禮葬焉。

translations.literal: Tiānxī recovered and mourned them, burying each with full wife ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: He survived and buried them as wives.

sentences.zh: 苻堅妾張氏

translations.literal: Concubine Zhāng of Fu Jiān
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhang, concubine of Fu Jian

sentences.zh: 苻堅妾張氏，不知何許人，明辯有才識。

translations.literal: Concubine Zhāng of Fu Jiān—homeland unknown—was lucid in debate and keen of judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian's concubine Lady Zhang—eloquent and wise.

sentences.zh: 堅將入寇江左，群臣切諫不從。

translations.literal: Jiān intended to invade the lands east of the Yangtze; ministers remonstrated urgently yet he refused.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian planned southern invasion despite court protests.

sentences.zh: 張氏進曰：「妾聞天地之生萬物，聖王之馭天下，莫不順其性而暢之，故黃帝服牛乘馬，因其性也，禹鑿龍門，決洪河，因水之勢也；

translations.literal: Lady Zhāng advanced saying, "I have heard that heaven and earth nurture the myriad things and sage kings steer all beneath heaven by smoothing each nature—thus the Yellow Emperor yoked oxen and rode horses according to their nature; Yǔ cut Dragon Gate and dredged the flooding Yellow River following water's momentum;
translations.idiomatic: She lectured on working with nature—Yellow Emperor tamed beasts, Yu dredged rivers.

sentences.zh: 后稷之播殖百穀，因地之氣也；

translations.literal: Hòujì broadcast the hundred grains according to earth's qi;
translations.idiomatic: Houji planted grain following soil's breath.

sentences.zh: 湯武之滅夏商，因人之欲也。

translations.literal: Tāng and Wǔ destroyed Xià and Shāng by riding human desire.
translations.idiomatic: Tang and Wu ended Xia and Shang by harnessing popular will.

sentences.zh: 是以有因成，無因敗。

translations.literal: Therefore success rides opportunity—failure rides its absence.
translations.idiomatic: Success follows alignment; disaster follows its lack.

sentences.zh: 今朝臣上下皆言不可，陛下復何所因也？

translations.literal: Now every minister high and low declares the venture unwise—on what ground does Your Majesty proceed?
translations.idiomatic: If every minister opposed invasion, what grounds remained?

sentences.zh: 書曰：'天聰明自我民聰明。

translations.literal: The Classic says: 'Heaven's keen hearing shares our people's hearing.'
translations.idiomatic: The Book says heaven hears through the people's ears.

sentences.zh: '天猶若此，況於人主乎！

translations.literal: Heaven behaves thus—how much more a mortal lord!
translations.idiomatic: If heaven listens so, what of emperors?

sentences.zh: 妾聞人君有伐國之志者，必上觀乾象，下采眾祥。

translations.literal: I have heard that rulers bent on aggressive war consult celestial signs above and gather auspices below.
translations.idiomatic: Conquerors read stars and omens.

sentences.zh: 天道崇遠，非妾所知。

translations.literal: Heaven's way is lofty—not for concubines to know.
translations.idiomatic: She disclaimed astronomy.

sentences.zh: 以人事言之，未見其可。

translations.literal: Judging human affairs I see no feasibility.
translations.idiomatic: Human signs looked ill.

sentences.zh: 諺言：「雞夜鳴者不利行師，犬群唕者宮室必空，兵動馬驚，軍敗不歸。

translations.literal: Proverbs say: 'Roosters crowing at night bode ill for marching; dogs baying in packs mean palaces will empty; armies stir when horses panic—defeat follows without return.
translations.idiomatic: Omens listed crowing flocks, howling dogs, stampeding stable horses.

sentences.zh: 」秋冬已來，每夜群犬大嗥，眾雞夜鳴，伏聞廄馬驚逸，武庫兵器有聲，吉凶之理，誠非微妾所論，願陛下詳而思之。

translations.literal: Since autumn and winter dogs nightly howl and fowls crow at midnight; I hear stable horses bolt and armory weapons clang—auspice or disaster lies beyond a concubine's reckoning—yet I beg Your Majesty ponder deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Since autumn dogs howled, roosters crowed at night, horses fled armories—she begged reflection.

sentences.zh: 」堅曰：「軍旅之事非婦人所豫也。

translations.literal: Jiān replied, "Campaign planning is no woman's province.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian dismissed warfare as no woman's affair.

sentences.zh: 」遂興兵。

translations.literal: He thereupon raised armies.
translations.idiomatic: He invaded anyway.

sentences.zh: 張氏請從。

translations.literal: Lady Zhāng requested to accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhang followed the host.

sentences.zh: 堅是大敗于壽春，張氏乃自殺。

translations.literal: Jiān suffered crushing defeat at Shòuchūn; Lady Zhāng then killed herself.
translations.idiomatic: After Shouchun disaster she killed herself.

sentences.zh: 竇滔妻蘇氏

translations.literal: Lady Sū, wife of Dòu Tāo
translations.idiomatic: Lady Su, wife of Dou Tao

sentences.zh: 竇滔妻蘇氏，始平人也，名蕙，字若蘭，善屬文。

translations.literal: The wife of Dòu Tāo, Lady Sū, came from Shiping—given name Huì, courtesy Ruòlán—skilled at composition.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Tao's wife Su Hui of Shiping—literary fame.

sentences.zh: 滔苻堅時為秦州刺史，被徙流沙，蘇氏思之，織錦為回文旋圖詩以贈滔。

translations.literal: Tāo served as Inspector of Qín province under Fu Jiān but was banished to shifting sands; Lady Sū longed for him and wove brocade into a palindrome poem in revolving graphs as gift.
translations.idiomatic: Banished to the desert, she wove reversible brocade verse for Dou Tao.

sentences.zh: 宛轉迴圈以讀之，詞甚淒惋，凡八百四十字，文多不錄。

translations.literal: Read winding and recursive—its language exceedingly mournful—eight hundred forty characters in all; the text is too long to transcribe here.
translations.idiomatic: Eight hundred forty characters read in cycles—too long to quote.

sentences.zh: 苻登妻毛氏

translations.literal: Lady Máo, wife of Fu Dēng
translations.idiomatic: Lady Mao, wife of Fu Deng

sentences.zh: 苻登妻毛氏，不知何許人，壯勇善騎射。

translations.literal: The wife of Fu Dēng, Lady Máo—homeland unknown—was robust, brave, skilled in riding and archery.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng's queen Lady Mao—warrior archer.

sentences.zh: 登為姚萇所襲，營壘既陷，毛氏猶彎弓跨馬，率壯士數百人，與萇交戰，殺傷甚眾。

translations.literal: When Dēng was ambushed by Yáo Cháng and camps fell, Lady Máo still bent her bow astride a horse, leading several hundred stalwarts to clash with Cháng, inflicting many casualties.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Chang stormed Fu Deng's camp she rode with bow, charging hundreds.

sentences.zh: 眾寡不敵，為萇所執。

translations.literal: Outnumbered, Cháng captured her.
translations.idiomatic: Numbers overcame her; Yao Chang seized her.

sentences.zh: 萇欲納之，毛氏罵曰：「吾天子-{后}-，豈為賊羌所辱，何不速殺我！

translations.literal: Cháng wished to take her; Lady Máo cursed, "I am consort of the Son of Heaven—could I suffer insult from bandit Qiang—kill me quickly!
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang meant to rape her; she screamed she was empress of heaven's son, not Qiang chattel.

sentences.zh: 」因仰天大哭曰：「姚萇無道，前害天子，今辱皇后，皇天后土，寧不鑒照！

translations.literal: She then lifted her face to heaven wailing, "Yáo Cháng lacks the Way—first he murdered the Son of Heaven, now he dishonors the empress—do imperial heaven and earthly soil not witness!
translations.idiomatic: She howled that Yao Chang slew her emperor and now shamed the queen—heaven must see.

sentences.zh: 」萇怒，殺之。

translations.literal: Cháng angrily executed her.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang executed her.

sentences.zh: 慕容垂妻段元妃

translations.literal: Lady Duàn Yuánfēi, wife of Mùróng Chuí
translations.idiomatic: Duan Yuanfei, wife of Murong Chui

sentences.zh: 慕容垂妻段氏，字元妃，偽右光祿大夫儀之女也。

translations.literal: The wife of Mùróng Chuí, Lady Duàn, courtesy Yuánfēi, was daughter of the Former Yan Right Household Grandee Duàn Yí.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui's wife Lady Duan Yuanfei—daughter of minister Duan Yi.

sentences.zh: 少而婉慧，有志操，常謂妹季妃曰：「我終不作凡人妻。

translations.literal: From youth she was gentle and clever, possessed of resolve; she often told younger sister Jìfēi, "I shall never end as an ordinary man's wife.
translations.idiomatic: She swore to her sister Duke Ji she would never marry a mediocrity.

sentences.zh: 」季妃亦曰：「妹亦不為庸夫婦。

translations.literal: Jìfēi likewise said, "This sister will not be a vulgar husband's mate.
translations.idiomatic: Her sister vowed the same.

sentences.zh: 」鄰人聞而笑之。

translations.literal: Neighbors hearing this laughed.
translations.idiomatic: Neighbors mocked their boasts.

sentences.zh: 垂之稱燕王，納元妃為繼室，遂有殊寵。

translations.literal: When Chuí claimed title Prince of Yan he took Yuánfēi as successor wife and favored her singularly.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui's Yan kingship made Lady Duan his queen-to-be with singular favor.

sentences.zh: 偽范陽王德亦娉季妃焉。

translations.literal: The Former Prince of Fànyáng Dé likewise married Jìfēi.
translations.idiomatic: Murong De wed the younger sister.

sentences.zh: 姊妹俱為垂、德之妻，卒如其志。

translations.literal: Sisters became wives to Chuí and Dé—exactly as they vowed.
translations.idiomatic: Both sisters wed Murong brothers as promised.

sentences.zh: 垂既僭位，拜為皇后。

translations.literal: Once Chuí usurped full majesty he invested her as empress.
translations.idiomatic: When he took the throne she became empress.

sentences.zh: 垂立其子寶為太子也，元妃謂垂曰：「太子姿質雍容，柔而不斷，承平則為仁明之主，處難則非濟世之雄，陛下托之以大業，妾未見克昌之美。

translations.literal: When Chuí established his son Bǎo as heir Yuánfēi told Chuí, "The crown prince's bearing is mild—soft yet indecisive—in peace he would be humane and bright; amid hardship he cannot be the hero who saves the age—Your Majesty entrusts him the great enterprise yet I perceive no omen of flourishing prosperity.
translations.idiomatic: She warned Murong Chui that crown prince Murong Bao was soft—in crisis he could not save Yan.

sentences.zh: 遼西、高陽二王，陛下兒之賢者，宜擇一以樹之。

translations.literal: Among the Princes of Liáoxī and Gāoyáng—your sons of talent—choose one to establish.
translations.idiomatic: She urged choosing between the worthy Liaoxi or Gaoyang princes.

sentences.zh: 趙王麟奸詐負氣，常有輕太子之心，陛下一旦不諱，必有難作。

translations.literal: Prince Zhào Lín is treacherous, arrogant, and ever underrates the heir—should Your Majesty pass, calamity will arise.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhao Murong Lin schemed against the heir—succession would spark coup.

sentences.zh: 此陛下之家事，宜深圖之。

translations.literal: This is household business of Your Majesty—ponder it deeply.
translations.idiomatic: She begged deep dynastic planning.

sentences.zh: 」垂不納。

translations.literal: Chuí did not heed her.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui ignored her.

sentences.zh: 寶及麟聞之，深以為恨。

translations.literal: Bǎo and Lín hearing this nursed deep resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Bao and Murong Lin nursed hatred.

sentences.zh: 其后元妃又言之，垂曰：「汝欲使我為晉獻公乎？

translations.literal: Later Yuánfēi spoke again; Chuí said, "Would you make me Marquis Xiàn of Jìn?
translations.idiomatic: When she repeated her warning he compared her to Jin's vicious concubine.

sentences.zh: 」元妃泣而退，告季妃曰：「太子不令，群下所知，而主上比吾為驪戎之女，何其苦哉！

translations.literal: Yuánfēi wept and withdrew, telling Jìfēi, "The heir lacks virtue—the realm knows—yet the sovereign classes me with Lí Róng's daughter—how bitter!
translations.idiomatic: She wept that Chui likened her to evil favorites though Bao was known weak.

sentences.zh: 主上百年之後，太子必亡社稷。

translations.literal: After the sovereign's hundred years the heir will surely lose the altars.
translations.idiomatic: After his death Bao would doom Yan.

sentences.zh: 范陽王有非常器度，若燕祚未終，其在王乎！」

translations.literal: The Prince of Fànyáng bears extraordinary capacity—if Yan's mandate lingers perhaps he inherits!"
translations.idiomatic: Lady Duan predicted Prince Murong De might salvage Yan.

sentences.zh: 垂死，寶嗣偽位，遣麟逼元妃曰：「-{后}-常謂主上不能嗣守大統，今竟何如？

translations.literal: After Chuí died Bǎo succeeded to false throne; he sent Lín to intimidate Yuánfēi: "You always claimed the sovereign could not guard the succession—how stands it now?
translations.idiomatic: Murong Bao succeeded; Murong Lin bullied her—had she not doubted him?

sentences.zh: 宜早自裁，以全段氏。

translations.literal: Better die early yourself to preserve the Duàn clan.
translations.idiomatic: Lin ordered suicide to save her clan.

sentences.zh: 」元妃怒曰：「汝兄弟尚逼殺母，安能保守社稷！

translations.literal: Yuánfēi angrily replied, "Your brotherhood would force a mother's death—how could you preserve the altars!
translations.idiomatic: She retorted that fratricidal sons could not hold Yan.

sentences.zh: 吾豈惜死，念國滅不久耳。

translations.literal: Do I cling to life—I grieve the realm's imminent ruin!
translations.idiomatic: She welcomed death mourning Yan's fall.

sentences.zh: 」遂自殺。

translations.literal: She thereupon killed herself.
translations.idiomatic: She took her life.

sentences.zh: 寶議以元妃謀廢嫡統，無母后之道，不宜成喪，群下咸以為然。

translations.literal: Bǎo debated posting that Yuánfēi plotted deposing the legitimate heir—lacking conduct befitting a dowager—proper mourning should not be observed; ministers agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Bao refused her funeral as unwomanly regicide plotter—court agreed.

sentences.zh: 偽中書令眭邃大言於朝曰：「子無廢母之義，漢之安思閻-{后}-親廢順帝，猶配饗安皇，先后言虛實尚未可知，宜依閻-{后}-故事。

translations.literal: False Secretariat Director Suì Suì proclaimed at court, "Sons may not disown mothers—even Hàn's Ānsī Empress Yān personally deposed Emperor Shùn yet shared Emperor Ān's sacrifice—first empress's charges remain unproved—follow Yān precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Su Sui cited Han Empress Yan who deposed Shun yet kept sacrifice—demanding Lady Duan receive rites.

sentences.zh: 」寶從之。

translations.literal: Bǎo accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Bao conceded proper burial.

sentences.zh: 其後麟果作亂，寶亦被殺，德后僭稱尊號，終如元妃之言。

translations.literal: Later Lín indeed rebelled—Bǎo likewise fell—and Dé's queen later usurped title—exactly as Yuánfēi foretold.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Lin rebelled, Murong Bao died, Murong De's queen seized style—as she predicted.

sentences.zh: 段豐妻慕容氏

translations.literal: Lady Mùróng, wife of Duàn Fēng
translations.idiomatic: Lady Murong, wife of Duan Feng

sentences.zh: 段豐妻慕容氏，德之女也。

translations.literal: The wife of Duàn Fēng, Lady Mùróng, was Dé's daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Feng's wife was Murong De's daughter.

sentences.zh: 有才慧，善書史，能鼓琴，德既僭位，署為平原公主。

translations.literal: Talented and clever, skilled in writing and history, able on the zither—once Dé usurped rank he styled her Princess of Pingyuán.
translations.idiomatic: Learned musician—Murong De named her Princess of Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 年十四，適於豐。

translations.literal: At fourteen she married Feng.
translations.idiomatic: She married Duan Feng at fourteen.

sentences.zh: 豐為人所譖，被殺，慕容氏寡歸，將改適偽壽光公餘熾。

translations.literal: Feng was slandered and executed; Lady Murong returned widowed and was to be remarried to the false Duke of Shòuguāng Yú Chì.
translations.idiomatic: Slander killed Duan Feng; Murong De's daughter faced forced marriage to Yu Chi.

sentences.zh: 慕容氏謂侍婢曰：「我聞忠臣不事二君，貞女不更二夫。

translations.literal: Lady Murong told her maids, "I have heard that loyal ministers serve no second lord and faithful wives take no second husband.
translations.idiomatic: She told servants faithful wives never remarry.

sentences.zh: 段氏既遭無辜，己不能同死，豈復有心於重行哉！

translations.literal: The Duàn clan already suffered wrongful doom—I could not die with them—how could I intend another marriage!
translations.idiomatic: Duan wrongs had not let her die with her lord—she still scorned a second match.

sentences.zh: 今主上不顧禮義嫁我，若不從，則違嚴君之命矣。

translations.literal: Now the sovereign would marry me off without regard to ritual; if I refuse I defy a stern parent's command.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Bao ignored propriety; refusal disobeyed her royal father.

sentences.zh: 」於是克日交禮。

translations.literal: She therefore set the wedding day for formal exchange of gifts.
translations.idiomatic: She fixed the ceremony date.

sentences.zh: 慕容氏姿容婉麗，服飾光華，熾睹之甚喜。

translations.literal: Lady Murong's bearing was gentle and lovely, her robes dazzling—Chì delighted in the sight.
translations.idiomatic: She dazzled Yu Chi in splendid dress.

sentences.zh: 經再宿，慕容氏偽辭以疾，熾亦不之逼。

translations.literal: After two nights she feigned illness; Chì did not force her.
translations.idiomatic: Two nights she pled sickness—Yu Chi did not press her.

sentences.zh: 三日還第，沐浴置酒，言笑自若，至夕，密書其裙帶云：「死後當埋我于段氏墓側，若魂魄有知，當歸彼矣。

translations.literal: On the third day she returned home, bathed, poured wine, chatted as though nothing were wrong; toward evening she secretly wrote on her sash: "Bury me beside the Duàn tomb—should soul endure it shall return there."
translations.idiomatic: Day three she banqueted calmly, then stitched her sash—bury her beside Duan Feng.

sentences.zh: 」遂於浴室自縊而死。

translations.literal: She then strangled herself in the bath chamber.
translations.idiomatic: She hanged herself in the bathroom.

sentences.zh: 及葬，男女觀者數萬人，莫不歎息曰：「貞哉公主！

translations.literal: At burial tens of thousands of men and women watched, every voice sighing, "How chaste the princess!
translations.idiomatic: Crowds thronged her funeral praising the princess's fidelity.

sentences.zh: 」路經餘熾宅前，熾聞輓歌之聲，慟絕良久。

translations.literal: The route passed before Chì's mansion; hearing dirges Chì sobbed until breath failed.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chi heard the lament outside his gate and collapsed.

sentences.zh: 呂纂妻楊氏

translations.literal: Lady Yáng, wife of Lǚ Zuǎn
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yang, wife of Lü Zuan

sentences.zh: 呂纂妻楊氏，弘農人也。

translations.literal: The wife of Lǚ Zuǎn, Lady Yáng, came from Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Zuan's wife Lady Yang of Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 美豔有義烈。

translations.literal: Lovely and fiercely principled.
translations.idiomatic: Beautiful and righteous.

sentences.zh: 纂被呂超所殺，楊氏與侍婢十數人殯纂於城西。

translations.literal: Zuǎn fell to Lǚ Chāo's blades; Lady Yáng with a dozen maids laid Zuǎn out west of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Chao murdered Zuan; Lady Yang buried him west of town.

sentences.zh: 將出宮，超慮齎珍物出外，使人搜之。

translations.literal: About to leave the palace Chāo feared she carried jewels out and sent men to search her.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Chao strip-searched her for treasure.

sentences.zh: 楊氏厲聲責超曰：「爾兄弟不能和睦，手刃相屠，我旦夕死人，何用金寶！

translations.literal: Lady Yáng sternly rebuked Chāo: "Your brothers could not live in harmony yet butcher one another—I am a corpse walking—what use have I for gold!
translations.idiomatic: She scolded that feuding Lü brothers needed no gold from a dying woman.

sentences.zh: 」超慚而退。

translations.literal: Chāo withdrew ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Chao slunk away shamed.

sentences.zh: 又問楊氏玉璽所在，楊氏怒曰：「盡毀之矣。

translations.literal: He again asked where the jade seal lay; Lady Yáng angrily said, "It is utterly destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: He demanded the seal; she swore it was smashed.

sentences.zh: 」超將妻之，謂其父桓曰：「后若自殺，禍及卿宗。

translations.literal: Chāo meant to marry her, telling her father Huán, "If the empress kills herself your clan will suffer.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Chao threatened her father: suicide would doom the Yangs.

sentences.zh: 」桓以告楊氏，楊氏曰：「大人本賣女與氏以圖富貴，一之已甚，其可再乎！

translations.literal: Huán reported this; Lady Yáng said, "Elder, you sold your daughter to the Lǚ for riches—once was excess—could it happen twice!
translations.idiomatic: She told father peddling her twice to the Lüs was unthinkable.

sentences.zh: 」乃自殺。

translations.literal: She thereupon killed herself.
translations.idiomatic: She killed herself.

sentences.zh: 時呂紹妻張氏亦有操行，年十四，紹死，便請為尼。

translations.literal: At that time Lǚ Shào's wife Lady Zhāng likewise maintained integrity—fourteen years old when Shào died she requested nunhood.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Shao's widow Lady Zhang, fourteen, took vows.

sentences.zh: 呂隆見而悅之，欲穢其行，張氏曰：「欽樂至道，誓不受辱。

translations.literal: Lǚ Lóng saw her and coveted her, plotting to stain her virtue; Lady Zhāng answered, "I delight in the supreme Way—I swear never to suffer dishonor.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Long lusted after her; she vowed the Dharma over shame.

sentences.zh: 」遂升樓自投於地，二脛俱折，口誦佛經，俄然而死。

translations.literal: She then mounted a tower and cast herself down—both shinbones shattered—yet chanting sutras until death followed swiftly.
translations.idiomatic: She leaped from a tower, broke both legs, chanted sutras, and died.

sentences.zh: 涼武昭王李玄盛后尹氏

translations.literal: Empress Lady Yǐn of Li Xuānshèng, Martial Illuminating Prince of Liáng
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yin, queen of Li Gao of Former Liang

sentences.zh: 涼武昭王李玄盛后尹氏，天水冀人也。

translations.literal: Empress Lady Yǐn of Li Xuānshèng, Martial Illuminating Prince of Liáng, came from Ji in Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gao's queen Lady Yin of Ji in Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 幼好學，清辯有志節。

translations.literal: From childhood she loved learning—lucid in debate and stalwart in resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Scholarly, eloquent, principled.

sentences.zh: 初適扶風馬元正，元正卒，為玄盛繼室。

translations.literal: She first married Mǎ Yuánzhèng of Fúfēng; when Yuánzhèng died she became Xuānshèng's successor wife.
translations.idiomatic: Widowed from Ma Yuanzheng, she married Li Gao as successor wife.

sentences.zh: 以再醮之故，三年不言。

translations.literal: Because this was a second marriage she did not speak for three years.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed of remarriage she kept silence three years.

sentences.zh: 撫前妻子逾于己生。

translations.literal: She nurtured the sons of the earlier wife more tenderly than her own.
translations.idiomatic: She favored Li Gao's prior sons over her own issue.

sentences.zh: 玄盛之創業也，謨謀經略多所毗贊，故西州諺曰：「李、尹王敦煌。」

translations.literal: During Xuānshèng's founding of the enterprise she aided stratagem and planning—hence the western frontier proverb: "The Lis and Yǐns king Dunhuáng."
translations.idiomatic: She shaped Li Gao's rise—westrons said Li and Yin ruled Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 及玄盛薨，子士業嗣位，尊為太后。

translations.literal: After Xuānshèng died his son Shìyè succeeded and honored her as dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gao died; son Li Xin elevated her as empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 士業將攻沮渠蒙遜，尹氏謂士業曰：「汝新造之國，地狹人稀，靖以守之猶懼其失，云何輕舉，窺冀非望！

translations.literal: When Shìyè planned to attack Jǔqú Méngxùn Lady Yǐn told him, "Your newly founded state—narrow land, sparse folk—quiet defense still fears loss—why rashly strike beyond hope!
translations.idiomatic: She warned Xin that tiny Former Liang could ill afford Juqu Mengxun.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜驍武，善用兵，汝非其敵。

translations.literal: Méngxùn is fierce in arms and clever in war—you are no match.
translations.idiomatic: Juqu Mengxun outclassed him militarily.

sentences.zh: 吾觀其數年已來有並兼之志，且天時人事似欲歸之。

translations.literal: I observe these several years he harbors annexation intent—heaven's seasons and human affairs alike incline toward him.
translations.idiomatic: Years of watching showed Mengxun's appetite for conquest.

sentences.zh: 今國雖小，足以為政。

translations.literal: Though our state is small it suffices for governance.
translations.idiomatic: Small Liang could still rule itself.

sentences.zh: 知足不辱，道家明誡也。

translations.literal: Contentment escapes insult—Daoism's plain lesson.
translations.idiomatic: Daoists prized knowing enough.

sentences.zh: 且先王臨薨，遺令殷勤，志令汝曹深慎兵戰，俟時而動。

translations.literal: Moreover the late king on his deathbed earnestly charged you to wield arms with deepest caution and await the hour.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gao's deathbed urged caution in war.

sentences.zh: 言猶在耳，柰何忘之！

translations.literal: His words still ring in the ears—how dare you forget!
translations.idiomatic: His voice still echoed—why ignore it?

sentences.zh: 不如勉修德政，蓄力以觀之。

translations.literal: Better cultivate virtue and husband strength while watching.
translations.idiomatic: Wait and build virtue.

sentences.zh: 彼若淫暴，人將歸汝；

translations.literal: Should he turn debauched the people will rally to you;
translations.idiomatic: If Mengxun turned cruel subjects would flock to Xin.

sentences.zh: 汝苟德之不建，事之無日矣。

translations.literal: If you fail to establish virtue opportunity will never come.
translations.idiomatic: Without virtue no opening would appear.

sentences.zh: 汝此行也，非唯師敗，國亦將亡。

translations.literal: This expedition means not only routed armies—a kingdom will perish.
translations.idiomatic: This march would doom army and state.

sentences.zh: 」士業不從，果為蒙遜所滅。

translations.literal: Shìyè refused heed and indeed fell to Méngxùn's destruction.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xin ignored her and Juqu Mengxun crushed him.

sentences.zh: 尹氏至姑臧，蒙遜引見勞之，對曰：「李氏為胡所滅，知復何言！

translations.literal: When Lady Yǐn reached Gūzàng Méngxùn granted audience and condoled; she answered, "The Li house perished to barbarians—what remains to say!
translations.idiomatic: Brought before Mengxun in Guzang she sneered that Li was gone.

sentences.zh: 」或諫之曰：「母子命懸人手，柰何倨傲！

translations.literal: Some cautioned her: "Mother and sons hang by others' whims—why arrogance!
translations.idiomatic: Advisors feared her pride endangered kin.

sentences.zh: 且國敗子孫屠滅，何獨無悲？

translations.literal: Moreover state ruin slaughtered posterity—why no grief?
translations.idiomatic: They asked why she showed no sorrow.

sentences.zh: 」尹氏曰：「興滅死生，理之大分，何為同凡人之事，起兒女之悲！

translations.literal: Lady Yǐn said, "Rise and fall, death and life—great patterns of principle—why mimic vulgar folk raising sentimental grief!
translations.idiomatic: She replied rise and fall were cosmic pattern—not petty tears.

sentences.zh: 吾一婦人，不能死亡，豈憚斧鉞之禍，求為臣妾乎！

translations.literal: I am one woman yet cannot seek death—would I dread axe and blade to beg servitude!
translations.idiomatic: She would not grovel to survive.

sentences.zh: 若殺我者，吾之願矣。

translations.literal: Let him kill me—that would be my wish.
translations.idiomatic: Death would satisfy her.

sentences.zh: 」蒙遜嘉之，不誅，為子茂虔娉其女為妻。

translations.literal: Méngxùn admired her and did not execute—married his son Màoqián to her daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun spared her and wed his son Maoqian to her girl.

sentences.zh: 及魏氏以武威公主妻茂虔，尹氏及女遷居酒泉。

translations.literal: Later the Wei clan married the Princess of Wǔwēi to Màoqián; Lady Yǐn and daughter moved to Jiǔquán.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei gave Maoqian Princess Wuwei; Lady Yin moved to Jiuquan.

sentences.zh: 既而女卒，撫之不哭，曰：「汝死晚矣！

translations.literal: Presently the daughter died; Lady Yǐn stroked her without weeping, saying, "You died too late!
translations.idiomatic: When her daughter died she refused tears—you died too late.

sentences.zh: 」沮渠無諱時鎮酒泉，每謂尹氏曰：「后諸孫在伊吾，后能去不？

translations.literal: Jǔqú Wúhuì then held Jiǔquán and often asked Lady Yǐn, "Your grandsons remain at Yīwú—can you depart?
translations.idiomatic: Juqu Wuhui asked whether she would join grandsons at Yiwu.

sentences.zh: 」尹氏未測其言，答曰：「子孫流漂，托身醜虜，老年餘命，當死於此，不能作氈裘鬼也。

translations.literal: Lady Yǐn unsure of his intent answered, "Grandsons drift rootless in barbarian hands—the remnant years of an old woman ought to die here—I cannot become a felt-tent ghost.
translations.idiomatic: She first refused to live as Hu hostage ghost.

sentences.zh: 」俄而潛奔伊吾，無諱遣騎追及之。

translations.literal: Shortly she secretly fled toward Yīwú; Wúhuì sent riders who overtook her.
translations.idiomatic: She fled toward Yiwu; Juqu Wuhui's riders caught her.

sentences.zh: 尹氏謂使者曰：」沮渠酒泉許我歸北，何故來追？

translations.literal: Lady Yǐn told envoys: "Jǔqu of Jiǔquán promised me passage north—why pursue?
translations.idiomatic: She challenged Juqu's pledge to let her go north.

sentences.zh: 汝可斬吾首歸，終不回矣。

translations.literal: You may carry my severed head back—I shall never return.
translations.idiomatic: Take her head—she would not turn back.

sentences.zh: 」使者不敢逼而還。

translations.literal: Envoys dared not press her and departed.
translations.idiomatic: They withdrew helpless.

sentences.zh: 年七十五，卒于伊吾。

translations.literal: At seventy-five she died at Yīwú.
translations.idiomatic: She died at seventy-five in Yiwu.

sentences.zh: 【史論】

translations.literal: 【Historians' Essay】
translations.idiomatic: Historians' commentary

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：夫繁霜降節，彰勁心於後凋；

translations.literal: The historians say: When heavy frost signals the season it manifests steadfast hearts that wither last;
translations.idiomatic: Historians write: frost reveals last-evergreens.

sentences.zh: 橫流在辰，表貞期於上德，匪伊尹子，抑亦婦人焉。

translations.literal: when floods surge in their hour they display faithful expectation toward supreme virtue—not those Yi-and-Yin exemplars alone—women likewise.
translations.idiomatic: In chaotic ages fidelity shines—not only great ministers but women.

sentences.zh: 自晉政陵夷，罕樹風檢，虧閑爽操，相趨成俗，薦之以劉石，汩之以苻姚。

translations.literal: Once Jin governance decayed few upheld moral scrutiny—loss of inner purity became fashion—Liu and Shi hastened it—Fu and Yao swept it along.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Jin's collapse brought moral slack—barbarian dynasties hastened decadence.

sentences.zh: 三月歌胡，唯見爭新之飾；

translations.literal: Third-month Hu tunes heard only contention for novel adornment;
translations.idiomatic: Frontier Hu fashions chased novelty.

sentences.zh: 一朝辭漢，曾微戀舊之情。

translations.literal: a morning's farewell to Han rarely showed longing for the old.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving Han lands none looked back.

sentences.zh: 馳騖風埃，脫落名教，頹縱忘反，於茲為極。

translations.literal: They galloped through dust storms, shrugged off ethical teaching—dissolute abandon peaked here.
translations.idiomatic: People fled Confucian restraint into reckless abandon.

sentences.zh: 至若惠風之數喬屬，道韞之對孫恩，荀女釋急於重圍，張妻報怨于強寇，僭登之后，蹈死不回，偽纂之妃，捐生匪吝，宗辛抗情而致夭，王靳守節而就終，斯皆冥踐義途，匪因教至。

translations.literal: Yet Huifeng scolded Qiao Shu, Daoyun defied Sun En, Xun's girl broke a tight siege, Zhang's wife avenged fierce raiders—Fu Deng's queen chose death unflinching, Lü Zuan's consort gave life unsparing—Zong and Xin met heaven early, Wang and Jin held faith to the end—all trod righteousness of their own hearts, not because teaching shaped them.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Wang Huifeng, Xie Daoyun, Xun Guan, Zhang Mao's widow, Fu Deng's warrior queen, Lü Zuan's Lady Yang, and others embodied virtue without awaiting sermons.

sentences.zh: 聳清漢之喬葉，有裕徽音；

translations.literal: They lift high branches of pure Han stock—echoing splendid fame;
translations.idiomatic: They honor Han purity with glorious names.

sentences.zh: 振幽谷之貞蕤，無慚雅引，比夫懸梁靡顧，齒劍如歸，異日齊風，可以激揚千載矣。

translations.literal: they rouse chaste blossoms from silent valleys—no shame beside refined precedent—beside those who faced beams without glance or tasted swords as home—another day's wind may inspire the thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: Their chastity rivals ancient rope-and-blade martyrs—future ages may thrill at their breeze.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：從容陰禮，婉娩柔則。

translations.literal: Encomium: Serene within women's ritual, gentle and yielding in woman's norm.
translations.idiomatic: Encomium: Grace within women's rites.

sentences.zh: 載循六行，爰昭四德。

translations.literal: They tread the six conducts and illuminate the four virtues.
translations.idiomatic: They walked the six feminine arts, lit the four virtues.

sentences.zh: 操潔風霜，譽流邦國。

translations.literal: Integrity frost-pure; praise floods every state.
translations.idiomatic: Purity like frost; fame crossed realms.

sentences.zh: 彤管貽訓，清芬靡忒。

translations.literal: Red tube traditions pass instruction—fragrance forever true.
translations.idiomatic: Their fragrance endures in women's histories.
